ipos.name: Mahanadi Coalfields
ipos.about:
Mahanadi Coalfields Limited is a coal mining company and a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Limited. The company primarily produces non-coking coal, including raw coal and washed coal, for power generation and industrial use. Its customers include state and private power utilities, captive power plants, independent power producers, and companies operating in the cement, steel, sponge iron, aluminium and paper industries.
The company operates in the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields in Odisha. As of September 30, 2026, it operated 17 mines, comprising 14 opencast mines and three underground mines. It also operates the Ib Valley Washery at Lakhanpur, with an annual processing capacity of 10 million tonnes. Its mining operations are supported by coal-handling plants, rapid loading systems, silos, and transportation infrastructure. 
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO is completely an offer for sale.​ The net proceeds from the issue will go to the selling shareholder, Coal India Ltd. The company will not get any proceeds from the IPO. The primary objective of the offer is to achieve the benefits of listing the equity shares on the stock exchanges, which is expected to enhance the company’s visibility and brand recognition. Listing will also provide liquidity to the existing shareholders and create a public market for the company’s shares in India​.
strengths: Mahanadi Coalfields was India's largest single coal-producing company in FY26, accounting for 21% of domestic coal production. As of April 1, 2026, the company had audited coal reserves of 9,840.31 million tonnes, estimated to support production for approximately 45 years at FY26 production levels.

The company had the lowest production cost per tonne among Coal India Limited's subsidiaries in FY26. Around 99.85% of its coal production came from opencast mines, while surface miners accounted for 99.37% of total production.

As of September 30, 2026, the company claimed to have deployed 74 surface miners, comprising 22 owned and 52 contracted machines. It operated 17 mines and a coal washery with an annual capacity of 10 million tonnes in Odisha.

The company has rail connectivity through three railway zones and access to five ports in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. Railways accounted for 65.28% of its total coal dispatch in FY26, compared to 58.70% in FY24, reducing its dependence on road transportation.

Mahanadi Coalfields supplied coal to customers across 16 Indian states in FY26. Its major customers include NTPC, Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation, and Tamil Nadu Power Generation Corporation, with whom it has maintained relationships for more than 15 years.

In FY26, the company reported an EBITDA margin of 47.45%, an operating EBITDA margin of 41.69% and a PAT margin of 31.56%, the highest among its listed industry peers. Its profit after tax stood at Rs 10,698.12 crore during the year.
risks: Raw non-coking coal accounted for 99.94%, 97.10%, and 97.41% of the company's revenue from sale of products in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Revenue from raw coal declined from Rs 31,190.41 crore in FY24 to Rs 29,600.64 crore in FY25 and Rs 29,081.22 crore in FY26. Any further decline in demand could affect the company's financial performance.

The thermal power sector contributed 69.41%, 70.60%, and 68.62% of the company's revenue from sale of products in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Revenue from this sector declined from Rs 21,663.66 crore in FY24 to Rs 21,521.79 crore in FY25 and Rs 20,485.41 crore in FY26. The company attributed the 4.82% decline in FY26 sales to the power sector, primarily to increased renewable energy contributions to the power grid.

The company's trade receivables increased from Rs 2,160.29 crore in FY24 to Rs 2,676.05 crore in FY25 and Rs 3,743.68 crore in FY26, despite declining revenue from operations. As of September 30, 2026, Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation and Andhra Pradesh Power Development Company together owed approximately Rs 2,432.04 crore. Any delay or failure in collecting these outstanding receivables could adversely affect the company's liquidity, working capital and cash flows.

The company's contingent liabilities stood at Rs 9,923.24 crore in FY24, Rs 10,122.21 crore in FY25 and Rs 8,506.23 crore in FY26, representing 61.56%, 55.18% and 39.80% of its net worth, respectively. These liabilities increased to Rs 12,513.29 crore, or 55.86% of net worth, as of September 30, 2026. They include tax disputes, government dues, and land compensation claims, which could affect its financial position if they materialise.

Mahanadi Coalfields relies on Coal India Limited for technical resources, executive manpower, and strategic support. Its executive employees are seconded from Coal India Limited, and changes in resource allocation or secondment terms could affect its operational stability and employee costs.

The company's top 10 customers contributed Rs 16,860.91 crore, Rs 17,467.89 crore, and Rs 17,088.85 crore to revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Their contribution represented 53.30%, 55.71%, and 55.94% of revenue during these years. The loss of major customers or a shift towards imported or captive coal could affect its sales.

The company's contractual expenses increased from Rs 5,861.71 crore in FY24 to Rs 7,141.67 crore in FY25 before declining to Rs 6,823.62 crore in FY26. Its top 10 contractors accounted for 42.62%, 47.83%, and 60.02% of contractual expenses during these years, respectively. Disruptions involving these contractors could delay coal extraction, overburden removal, and transportation activities.

The company recorded six fatal accident cases in FY24, three in FY25 and three in FY26, with total compensation payable of approximately Rs 1.69 crore, Rs 0.90 crore and Rs 0.93 crore, respectively. It recorded one additional fatal accident case in the six months ended September 30, 2026. Such incidents could result in compensation liabilities, regulatory action, and suspension of mining operations.

The company's balance mineable reserves declined from 9,417.84 million tonnes in FY24 to 9,192.67 million tonnes in FY25 and 9,007.65 million tonnes in FY26. The company does not systematically re-estimate reserves at producing mines, and its resource estimates prepared under Indian Standard Procedure guidelines are not directly comparable with certain international standards.

The company, its subsidiaries, promoters, and directors are involved in certain ongoing legal proceedings. Any adverse judgments in any of these cases could be detrimental to the company’s business prospects.

The company recorded negative cash flows from investing activities amounting to Rs 5,067.99 crore in FY26 and Rs 3,432.66 crore in the six months ended September 30, 2026. It also recorded negative cash flows from financing activities of Rs 9,002.02 crore, Rs 8,600.84 crore, and Rs 7,651.21 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Sustained cash outflows exceeding inflows could adversely affect the company's liquidity, financial flexibility, and ability to fund future operations.

ipos.name: Watrana Rentals
ipos.about:
Watrana Rentals Limited provides material handling equipment (MHE) and aerial work platforms (AWP) on a rental basis. The company also trades in new and used material handling equipment and batteries used in such equipment.
Its rental fleet includes diesel and electric forklifts, reach trucks, battery-operated stackers, pallet trucks, order pickers, towing trucks, and aerial work platforms. The company also provides equipment operators, maintenance support, and replacement equipment as part of its rental arrangements, depending on customer requirements.
Watrana Rentals serves customers across industries, including automotive, tyres, food and beverages, glass, paper, manufacturing, logistics, and warehousing. It deploys its equipment at customer locations across India.
As of June 30, 2026, the company owned 2,679 MHE and AWP units, comprising 2,646 material handling equipment units and 33 aerial work platforms. Its registered office is located in Delhi.
strengths: As of June 30, 2026, Watrana Rentals reported owning 2,679 material handling equipment (MHE) and aerial work platform (AWP) units. Its fleet includes diesel and electric forklifts, reach trucks, pallet trucks, stackers, order pickers, and towing trucks, allowing it to serve different equipment requirements across industries.

As of June 30, 2026, the company provided rental and related services across 515 rental sites in 24 Indian states. This wide geographical presence allows it to serve customers across different regions and reduces dependence on any single operating location.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for Quality Management Systems, ISO 14001:2015 certified for Environmental Management Systems, and ISO 45001:2018 certified for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems. These certifications cover its rental and annual maintenance contract services for material handling equipment.

The company reported employing 3,883 personnel, including equipment operators, technicians, engineers, site supervisors, and managerial staff. It also claims to conduct internal induction and refresher training covering equipment handling, maintenance, safety procedures, and site-specific operating requirements.

The company's owned MHE and AWP fleet increased from 1,089 units in FY24 to 1,410 units in FY25 and 2,549 units in FY26, reaching 2,679 units as of June 30, 2026. This expansion has increased the equipment available for deployment across its rental operations.

The company has expanded beyond traditional material handling equipment by introducing aerial work platforms into its rental fleet. This enables it to address customer requirements for equipment used to perform work at elevated locations.

The company has reported consistent growth in its revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 130.12 crore in FY24 to Rs 179.48 crore in FY25 and Rs 211.36 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 18.05 crore in FY24 to Rs 24.43 crore in FY25 and Rs 29.16 crore in FY26.
risks: Watrana Rentals derives a substantial portion of its revenue from renting material handling equipment and aerial work platforms. Rental income stood at Rs 120.29 crore (92.45%) in FY24, Rs 162.36 crore (90.46%) in FY25, Rs 185.27 crore (87.66%) in FY26, and Rs 50.11 crore (93.72%) for the three months ended June 30, 2026. Any decline in demand for these rental services could adversely affect the company's revenue and profitability.

The company's top 10 customers contributed Rs 41.46 crore (31.86%) in FY24, Rs 48.29 crore (26.90%) in FY25, Rs 54.33 crore (25.70%) in FY26 and Rs 18.03 crore (33.73%) during the three months ended June 30, 2026. Any failure to retain these customers or a significant reduction in business from them could adversely affect the company's revenue and financial performance.

As of June 30, 2026, Watrana Rentals had total outstanding borrowings of Rs 164.72 crore. A default in repayment or non-compliance with loan covenants could result in lenders taking action against the company's secured assets, including material handling equipment. This could disrupt its operations and adversely affect its financial condition.

During FY26, the company acquired 642 material handling equipment units from Watrana Traction Company, a promoter group entity, without executing a formal purchase agreement or generating e-way bills. Although the company states that the transactions involved no physical movement of equipment, any adverse regulatory determination regarding documentation or GST compliance could affect its financial condition and operations.

The company has reported instances of non-filing, delayed filing, and inaccuracies in statutory forms submitted under the Companies Act, 2013. The disclosed filing delays ranged from 3 to 93 days, and certain charge-related forms were not filed. Such non-compliance could expose the company to penalties, regulatory scrutiny, and reputational risks.

The company, its subsidiaries, promoters, and directors are involved in certain ongoing legal proceedings. Any adverse judgments in any of these cases could be detrimental to the company’s business prospects.

The company reported attrition rates of 96.20% in FY24, 111.03% in FY25, and 86.54% in FY26 among its skilled and unskilled employees. Employee benefit expenses amounted to Rs 54.26 crore (41.66% of total income), Rs 77.66 crore (43.23%) and Rs 91.27 crore (43.12%) during these financial years, respectively. Continued high attrition could increase recruitment and training costs and disrupt equipment deployment at customer sites.

The company changed its depreciation method from Written Down Value (WDV) to Straight-Line Method (SLM) effective April 1, 2023. This reduced depreciation expenses by Rs 12.06 crore and increased net profit by approximately Rs 12.04 crore in FY24. The change materially affected reported profitability and may limit the comparability of financial results across periods.

Watrana Rentals reported negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 52.63 crore in FY24, Rs 43.39 crore in FY25, and Rs 91.39 crore in FY26. The negative cash flow continued at Rs 15.16 crore during the three months ended June 30, 2026, primarily reflecting expenditure on property, plant, and equipment. Continued capital expenditure could increase the company's dependence on operating cash flows and external financing to fund its expansion.

ipos.name: Zepto
ipos.about: Zepto Limited is the fastest-growing quick commerce platform in India, focused on delivering groceries, fruits, vegetables, and a wide assortment of household products to users in under 10 minutes. The company operates a marketplace model, leveraging a network of over 1,139 strategically located 'dark stores' as of March 2026. Its business model relies on a proprietary technology stack for its app, warehouse management, last-mile delivery, and brand advertising, serving both end-consumers and providing B2B services to wholesalers and retailers.
strengths: As India's fastest-growing quick commerce platform, Zepto's order volume grew at a CAGR of approximately 119.50% between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026, significantly outpacing the industry. This market leadership is mirrored in its financial performance, with revenue from operations skyrocketing from ₹4,454.52 Crores in FY24 to ₹22,623.58 Crores in FY26.

The company's 'densification flywheel' strategy is improving operational efficiency, evidenced by the Average Distance per Order decreasing from 2.05 km in FY24 to 1.78 km in FY26, while the Orders Per Day (OPD) per store increased from 1,325 to 1,677 in the same period.

Zepto is demonstrating significant improvements in unit economics, with Fixed Cost per Order reducing from ₹80.72 in Q1 FY24 to ₹52.34 in Q4 FY26. Concurrently, Digital Marketing Cost per Order has dramatically decreased from ₹10.82 to ₹1.01 in the same period, indicating increased brand salience and user retention.

The company is successfully monetizing its platform beyond delivery commissions, with high-margin Advertisement Revenue growing exponentially from ₹49.17 Crores in FY24 to ₹1,635.73 Crores in FY26, a CAGR of 477.9%. This segment now constitutes 7.23% of total revenue from operations in FY26.

Leveraging its data flywheel, Zepto has rapidly expanded its product assortment to enhance user engagement, increasing the average number of SKUs at a dark store from 12,312 in FY24 to 46,623 in FY26. This has deepened user adoption, with retained users purchasing from over 18 product categories within two years of joining.

The company has demonstrated strong user base growth, with Annual Transacting Users (ATU) growing from 10.57 million in FY24 to 47.97 million in FY26. This growth is supported by solid user retention, with 45.2% to 49.8% of users remaining active on the platform three years after their first order.

The company is led by its entrepreneurial founders, Aadit Palicha and Kaivalya Vohra, who are deeply involved in granular day-to-day execution. They are supported by an experienced management team with backgrounds in e-commerce, manufacturing, and retail from companies like Flipkart, ITC, and Amazon.

Zepto has rapidly executed its physical infrastructure expansion, growing its network of dark stores from 337 in FY24 to 1,139 in FY26. This aggressive rollout supports its densification strategy and ability to maintain fast delivery times while scaling order volumes.
risks: The company has a history of significant and growing losses, with restated loss for the year increasing from ₹1,214.79 Crores in FY24 to ₹5,905.19 Crores in FY26. It has also consistently generated negative cash flows from operating activities since its inception.

Business growth is critically dependent on acquiring and retaining users, which has historically required significant marketing expenditure. Advertisement expenses increased from ₹303.55 Crores in FY24 to ₹1,389.12 Crores in FY26, representing 6.14% of revenue from operations in the latest fiscal year.

The business model is heavily reliant on a non-exclusive 'gig economy' network of delivery partners and a wide base of merchant partners. In FY26, delivery and handling expenses amounted to ₹3,046.34 Crores, highlighting a major cost center and dependency for its core service.

The company faces intense competition from well-established players and new entrants in a market with low barriers to entry. Key competitors include Blinkit, a subsidiary of the publicly listed Zomato (Eternal Limited), and Instamart, a division of Swiggy, which have deep pockets and established ecosystems.

The company and its Promoters are involved in multiple pending litigations, including a penalty of ₹0.07 Crores from the CCPA for 'dark patterns', which is currently under appeal, and summons received by Promoters from the Directorate of Enforcement regarding FEMA inquiries. Total contingent liabilities from pending litigations are valued at ₹2.01 Crores.

The company experiences very high employee attrition, especially among its operational staff. The overall attrition rate was 51.28% in FY26, while the rate for its crucial 'Operating Staff' (pickers, packers, etc.) was significantly higher at 73.22% for the same period.

ipos.name: Razorpay
ipos.about: Razorpay is a Bengaluru-based financial technology company established in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar. It operates as a provider of comprehensive financial infrastructure and payment solutions for businesses, ranging from early-stage startups and small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) to large-scale corporations.

ipos.name: Truhome Finance
ipos.about: Truhome Finance Limited (formerly known as Shriram Housing Finance Limited) is a premier affordable housing finance company (HFC) in India, currently the third-largest in its segment by Assets Under Management (AUM). Following its acquisition by global private equity firm Warburg Pincus in December 2024, the Mumbai-based firm rebranded to Truhome to align with its new strategic positioning. As of December 31, 2025, the company reported an AUM of ₹21,124.32 crore, serving a predominantly self-employed customer base through a pan-India network of 216 branches across 19 states. Financially, the company has exhibited strong growth, recording a Total Income of ₹1,905.48 crore and a Profit After Tax (PAT) of ₹286.24 crore for FY25, maintained by a healthy asset quality with Net Stage-3 assets at 1.09%. The proposed ₹3,000 crore IPO consists of an equal split between a fresh issue of ₹1,500 crore and an Offer for Sale (OFS) of ₹1,500 crore by promoter Mango Crest Investment Ltd. The proceeds are primarily earmarked for augmenting the capital base to meet future lending requirements and ensuring strict compliance with RBI’s capital adequacy norms.

ipos.name: Marri Retail
ipos.about: Marri Retail Limited is a prominent Hyderabad-based multi-brand retailer specializing in apparel and jewelry, operating through well-known regional brands such as The Chennai Shopping Mall, JC Brothers, JC Mall, and Jeans Corner. From its origins as a small proprietorship in 1997, the company has scaled to a network of 34 stores (spanning nearly 0.98 million sq. ft.) across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Maharashtra. Financially, the company has shown significant momentum, reporting Revenue from Operations of ₹2,456.3 crore in FY25 and a Net Profit of ₹83.5 crore for the six-month period ending September 30, 2025. The IPO features a fresh issue of up to ₹522 crore and an Offer for Sale (OFS) of 2.7 crore equity shares by promoter Marri Venkat Reddy. Strategically, the company plans to utilize ₹250.5 crore of the proceeds for aggressive physical expansion (including 10 new apparel and 2 standalone jewelry stores) and ₹115.6 crore for debt repayment, aiming to strengthen its balance sheet as it transitions into a larger corporate retail entity.

ipos.name: InCred Holdings
ipos.about: InCred Holdings Limited (“formerly known as KKR Capital Markets Limited) (“InCred Holdings” / “IHL”) was incorporated on 3rd January, 2011 under the Companies Act, 1956 and holds a certificate of registration under Securities and Exchange Board of India (Merchant Bankers) Regulations, 1992, to act as a Merchant Banker bearing registration no. INM000011880, and also acts as an investment manager to certain alternative investment funds registered with SEBI under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012.

ipos.name: Hero Fincorp
ipos.about:
Hero Fincorp is a non-banking financial company (NBFC) that provides a range of financial services to retail customers and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in India. Its offerings include vehicle loans (two-wheeler, used car, and electric vehicle loans), personal loans, mortgage loans, and MSME financing (secured and unsecured loans for business needs). Hero Fincorp also offers loans to corporate and institutional customers. 
The company operates under the "Hero" brand and leverages the extensive distribution network of its parent company, Hero MotoCorp, which has a wide dealer presence across India. Hero Fincorp utilises a digital platform for customer acquisition and loan management. 
The company is headquartered in India and has an extensive presence across the country with a combination of in-house teams and distribution partnerships.
Use of proceeds:
The IPO consists of both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS).​ Proceeds from the OFS will go to the respective selling shareholders, whereas the net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​ 
Augmenting the company’s Tier-I capital to support future lending requirements.
Covering expenses related to the offer.
strengths: Hero Fincorp claims to have strategically expanded its product portfolio beyond two-wheeler loans to include a wide range of secured and unsecured loans, catering to both retail and MSME customers. As of FY24, retail and MSME loans accounted for 65.08 percent and 20.80 percent of its total assets under management (AUM).

Hero Fincorp claims to benefit from a deep-rooted relationship with Hero MotoCorp Limited, leveraging its brand recognition and extensive dealer network. In FY24, Hero MotoCorp Limited held a 41.19 percent equity stake in Hero Fincorp and provided financing for a significant portion of Hero MotoCorp’s two-wheeler sales.

The company claims to have developed a comprehensive, omnichannel distribution network that spans 18,603 pin-codes across India, aided by both digital and physical channels. Hero Fincorp also claims to source a substantial portion of its business through partnerships with 3,612 partners, including used car dealers, digital partners, and direct sales agents (DSAs).

Hero Fincorp claims to follow a ‘customer first approach’ that allows it to design customised products for retail and MSME clients, addressing unique financing needs across metro, urban, and rural regions. The company further states this approach enhances cross-sell potential, as demonstrated by a product per customer (PPC) ratio of 4.25 in FY24, 3.15 in FY23, and 3.52 in FY22.

The company claims to integrate technology seamlessly into customer onboarding, underwriting, loan servicing, and collections, providing a fully digital experience. It claims to leverage artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and real-time analytics to improve customer acquisition, reduce wait times, and streamline operations, boosting both operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.

The company claims to have consistently improved its asset quality over the years. As of FY24, the gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio is 4.02 percent, a reduction from 5.11 percent in FY23 and 7.54 percent in 2022. Similarly, the net non-performing assets (NNPA) ratio has declined to 2.00 percent in 2024, compared to 2.69 percent in 2023 and 4.43 percent in 2022.

Leveraging advanced data analytics, Hero Fincorp claims to enhance its risk management by tracking credit trends and predicting default probabilities. It has integrated a technology-driven collections infrastructure, improving efficiency with a 94.42 percent collection rate in FY24, 95.07 percent in FY23, and 83.00 percent in FY22, through mobile app-based repayments and a four-tier collections team.
The company claims to maintain a well-balanced mix of short-term and long-term assets and liabilities, minimising liquidity and interest rate risks.

The company has received credit ratings of AA+ with a stable outlook from Credit Rating Information Services of India Limited (CRISIL), Investment Information and Credit Rating Agency of India Limited (ICRA), and Credit Analysis and Research Limited (CARE), and an A1+ rating for commercial papers from CRISIL, CARE, and ICRA as of FY24.
The company has witnessed a consistent increase in revenue from operations. It increased from Rs 4,738.65 crore in FY22 to Rs 6,401.59 crore in FY23 and Rs 8,290.90 crore in FY24.
risks: Hero Fincorp sourced Rs 9,581.62 crore (99.04 percent), Rs 8,726.52 crore (99.69 percent), and Rs 8,074.88 crore (99.93 percent) of its two-wheeler loans from Hero MotoCorp Limited’s dealerships in FY24, FY23, and FY22, respectively. Any decline in demand for Hero MotoCorp’s two-wheelers could adversely affect the company’s ability to generate revenue from these loans, thereby impacting its business, results of operations, and financial condition.

The company’s retail finance business depends heavily on new-to-credit (NTC) borrowers. They accounted for 8.953.66 crore (26.55 percent) of the company’s total retail AUM in FY24, Rs 8,934.51 crore (34.06 percent) in FY23, and Rs 9,250.4 crore (46.33 percent) in FY22. The lack of credit history makes it difficult to assess these customers’ creditworthiness, which may result in higher default rates. In the event of defaults, recovering these loans, especially unsecured ones, could be challenging, potentially leading to the company’s financial losses.

Retail finance, including vehicle, personal, mortgage, and MSME loans, accounted for Rs 44,506.08 crore (85.88 percent) of the company’s total AUM in FY24, Rs 34,713.74 crore (83.14 percent) in FY23, and Rs 26,117.92 crore (79.02 percent) in FY22. Furthermore, as of FY24, 72.20 percent of these loans are extended to customers in the “Aspiring India” segment, who are vulnerable to economic downturns. Any adverse economic developments could reduce loan demand or increase default rates, negatively impacting the company’s financial condition.
The company’s promoters are involved in certain regulatory proceedings. Any adverse outcomes in these cases could be detrimental to the company’s reputation.

The company’s operations heavily depend on its information technology (IT) systems, which manage risk, deposit servicing, loan origination, and other critical functions. Capital expenditure incurred towards IT systems constituted Rs 48.43 crore (29.48 percent) of the company’s total expenditure in FY24, Rs 26.47 crore (57.51 percent) in FY23, and Rs 18.43 crore (71.79 percent) in FY22. Any internal or external disruptions, system failures, or inadequate maintenance could significantly affect customer service, operations, and the company’s reputation.

The company’s net interest income and margins are vulnerable to fluctuations in interest rates due to its fixed and floating-rate loans and borrowings. As of FY24, FY23, and FY22, Rs 37,084.04 crore (72.03 percent), Rs 31,352.22 crore (75.55 percent), and Rs 25,279.18 crore (76.72 percent) of total gross loans were extended at fixed interest rates. If interest rates rise, the company may not be able to fully pass on increased costs to fixed-rate borrowers, which could lead to lower margins, increased defaults, and reduced loan demand.

As of FY24, FY23, and FY22, unsecured loans accounted for Rs 20,275.58 crore (39.13 percent), Rs 15,521.04 crore (37.18 percent), and Rs 10,497.72 crore (31.76 percent) of the company’s total AUM, respectively. Any failure to recover receivables from these loans could adversely affect the company’s operations, cash flow, and financial condition.

The company is exposed to risks related to the devaluation or loss of collateral backing secured loans, such as property and vehicles. Secured loans accounted for Rs 30,866.24 crore (59.95 percent) of the company’s total gross loans in FY24, Rs 25,928.95 crore (62.48 percent) in FY23, and Rs 22,240.08 crore (67.49 percent) in FY22.

The company relies heavily on third-party distributors, including two-wheeler dealers, digital partners, and direct selling agents (DSAs). They accounted for 62.07 percent, 65.69 percent, and 58.02 percent of the company’s disbursements in FY24, FY23, and FY22, respectively. Any breakdown in relationships, service disruptions, or inefficiencies by these third-party service providers could impact the company’s business operations, financial condition, and reputation.

The company reported negative cash flow from operating activities amounting to Rs 9,238.83 crore in FY24, Rs 6,918.52 crore in FY23, and Rs 5,411.77 crore in FY22. Additionally, negative cash flow from investing activities amounted to Rs 129.79 crore in FY24 and Rs 474.13 crore in FY23. Furthermore, the company experienced a net decrease in cash and cash equivalents amounting to Rs 651.36 crore in FY24, Rs 124.35 crore in FY23, and Rs 232.37 crore in FY22. If cash outflows continue to exceed inflows in the future, the company may face liquidity challenges.
As of June 30, 2024, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 43,917.86 crore. Any failure to service or repay these loans can hurt the company’s operations and financial position.

ipos.name: Allchem Lifescience
ipos.about: Allchem Lifescience is an Indian company founded in 2003 by Mr. Bipin Patel, specializing in the manufacture of advanced pharmaceutical intermediates (API intermediates) and specialty chemicals. Headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat, Allchem Lifescience operates ISO-certified facilities and focuses on serving pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and industrial clients both in India and internationally across over 20 countries.

ipos.name: CarDekho
ipos.about: CarDekho is a leading Indian technology company founded in 2008 by brothers Amit Jain and Anurag Jain in Jaipur, Rajasthan. It operates digital platforms focused on automotive sales, reviews, insurance, and financing. Originally started as an online portal providing car reviews, specifications, and price comparisons to simplify buying and selling cars, CarDekho has evolved into a comprehensive automotive ecosystem.

ipos.name: Haldiram's Snacks Foods
ipos.about: Haldiram's is a renowned Indian food company that originated in 1937 as a small sweets and snacks shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan, founded by Ganga Bishan Agarwal, fondly known as Haldiram Ji. Over the decades, it has grown into one of India's largest and most trusted snack brands, with a diverse product range including traditional sweets, namkeens (savory snacks), papads, and cookies, alongside a strong presence in the restaurant and hospitality sectors.

ipos.name: Prestige Hospitality
ipos.about: Prestige Hospitality Ventures Ltd is a hospitality asset owner and developer focused on luxury, upper-upscale, and upper midscale hospitality assets in India. It caters to both business and leisure travelers and operates as part of the larger Prestige Group, which is promoted by Prestige Estates Projects Limited (PEPL)—a well-established real estate company with over 38 years of experience.

ipos.name: Curefoods
ipos.about:
Based in Bengaluru, Curefoods is a leading Indian food technology company that operates on a "house of brands" model, primarily through a vast network of cloud kitchens. Founded in 2020 by Ankit Nagori, the company's core strategy is to acquire, incubate, and scale a diverse portfolio of food brands.

Curefoods has grown rapidly by taking over popular brands and expanding their reach through its extensive operational infrastructure. Its portfolio covers a wide range of cuisines and includes well-known names such as:
EatFit (healthy meals)
Sharief Bhai (biryani)
Nomad Pizza and Olio (pizzas)
CakeZone (desserts)
Frozen Bottle (milkshakes and desserts)
The company operates hundreds of outlets, including cloud kitchens and physical restaurants, across numerous Indian cities.

ipos.name: Cult Fit
ipos.about: Cult.fit is a leading Indian health and fitness company headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Co-founded in 2016 by Mukesh Bansal and Ankit Nagori, the company's core mission is to make fitness fun, accessible, and a part of everyday life by offering a holistic approach to well-being.

ipos.name: Kent RO
ipos.about:
Kent R O Systems is a company engaged in the manufacturing and sale of water purifiers and household appliances. It offers a wide range of products, including electric and non-electric water purifiers, water softeners, internet of things (IoT)-enabled devices, zero-water-wastage systems, kitchen appliances, and brushless direct current (BLDC) fans under the brands ‘Kent’ and ‘Kuhl’. The product portfolio also includes items such as egg boilers, mixers, cooktops, multicookers, and vegetable cleaners.
The company operates four manufacturing facilities: one is situated in Roorkee, Uttarakhand, and the remaining three are located in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. The Roorkee unit focuses on water purifiers and softeners, while the Noida facilities handle the production of purifiers, appliances, and fans. One of the three facilities located in Noida also serves as a mother warehouse.
Use of proceeds:
The IPO is an offer-for-sale (OFS). The company will not receive any proceeds from the offer. Net proceeds from the offer will go to the promoter selling shareholders in proportion to the number of shares offered by them for sale.
The primary objective of the offer is to achieve the benefits of listing the equity shares on the stock exchanges, which is expected to enhance the company’s visibility and brand recognition. Listing will also provide liquidity to the existing shareholders and create a public market for the company’s shares in India​.
strengths: Kent R O Systems claims to be the pioneer in introducing reverse osmosis (RO) technology in the water purifier segment in India. The company first launched an RO-based water purifier in 1999 and claims to serve over 5.50 million consumers, as of September 30, 2024. The company further claims it has the highest number of stock-keeping units (SKUs) in both the overall and premium water purifier categories, among its peers.

The company claims to have received the highest number of certifications in the Indian water purifier category, including National Sanitation Foundation/American National Standards Institute standard for point-of-use reverse osmosis systems (NSF/ANSI 58), Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS ), Water Quality Association (WQA) gold seal certification, and CE (Conformité Européenne) marking.

The company claims to have a strong focus on innovation, with several patented technologies across its product portfolio. These include mineral RO technology, zero-water-wastage systems, IoT-enabled purifiers, and integrated ultraviolet light-emitting diodes (UV LEDs) for disinfection. Kent also claims to hold rights to use 15 registered patents and has a dedicated R&D lab in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, backed by a team of qualified professionals.

Kent R O Systems claims to have undertaken targeted brand-building initiatives aimed at enhancing brand equity and increasing visibility across multiple consumer touchpoints. The company’s marketing strategy spans television (TV) sponsorships, cricket team and tournament partnerships, print advertisements, digital media, social media, e-commerce platforms, over-the-top (OTT) mobile apps, and celebrity endorsements, notably with actress Hema Malini as its brand ambassador for over a decade.

Kent R O Systems claims to have the capability to build and scale new brands beyond its core water purification business. In FY23, it introduced its BLDC fan business under the ‘Kuhl’ brand and claims to have launched over 120 SKUs within two years. The company also claims to have established a dedicated fan manufacturing unit, Noida Facility II, with a built-up area of approximately 31,167 square metres.

Kent R O Systems claims to leverage its brand strength to offer a diverse product portfolio and increase consumer wallet share. While it is primarily known for RO water purifiers, the company has expanded into categories such as water softeners, kitchen and home appliances, and energy-efficient fans, under the ‘Kent’ and ‘Kuhl’ brands, respectively. It claims that this strategic diversification allows it to meet broader household needs and tap into multiple consumer spending categories.

Kent R O Systems claims to have streamlined manufacturing operations that combine in-house production with external sourcing to maintain product quality and efficiency. It further claims to use advanced machinery and quality control processes, including manufacturing key components like RO membranes and BLDC motors in-house.

Kent R O Systems claims to maintain a strong financial position, with significant reserves and no long-term debt since incorporation. The company states that it has built reserves through retained earnings, held in the form of cash equivalents, investments, and real estate assets. It also claims to follow a proactive inventory management approach and has invested in operational and residential real estate, some of which is provided to employees at no cost to support retention. As of September 30, 2024, the company reports holding Rs 477.51 crore in operational real estate, Rs 125.63 crore in residential real estate, and Rs 259.80 crore in investments.

The company claims to have a wide pan-India distribution and service network with 1,898 channel partners, 5,000+ technicians, and presence across 15,000+ pin codes. It also claims to be the largest exporter of water purifiers from India in FY24.

The company holds ISO 9001:2015 certification for quality management systems, ISO 14001:2015 certification for environmental management systems, and ISO 45001:2018 certification for occupational health and safety.
The company has witnessed a consistent increase in revenue from operations. It increased from Rs 1,047.37 crore in FY22 to Rs 1,084.39 crore in FY23 and Rs 1,178.18 crore in FY24.
risks: A substantial portion of the company’s revenue is derived from the sale of water purifiers and water softener products. They accounted for Rs 536.80 crore (84.25 percent) of the company’s revenue in the period ended September 30, 2024, Rs 1,012.42 crore (85.93 percent) in FY24, Rs 940.67 crore (86.75 percent) in FY23, and Rs 909.98 crore (86.88 percent) in FY22. Any decrease in demand for these products could hit the company’s business and finances.

The cost of raw materials consumed accounted for Rs 234.29 crore (39.40 percent) of the company’s total expenses in the period ended September 30, 2024, Rs 401.51 crore (38.62 percent) in FY24, Rs 365.69 crore (37.43 percent) in FY23, and Rs 340.24 crore (38.73 percent) in FY22. Any disruption in the supply of raw materials or fluctuations in raw material prices could adversely affect the company’s ability to manufacture its products, thereby negatively impacting its business, results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows.

A significant portion of Kent R O Systems’ raw material purchases are dependent on imports. They accounted for Rs 104.76 crore (43.02 percent) of the company’s total purchase of raw materials in the period ended September 30, 2024, Rs 149.02 crore (39.17 percent) in FY24, Rs 145.84 crore (36.29 percent) in FY23, and Rs 136.38 crore (37.59 percent) in FY22. Any restrictions on imports, an increase in duties, or geopolitical tensions in supplier regions can adversely impact the company’s business and profitability.
Three out of Kent R O Systems’ four manufacturing facilities are located in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Any disruption in this region can negatively impact the company’s business and finances.

Kent R O Systems relies heavily on its network of 1,898 channel partners as of September 30, 2024, for the distribution of its products. Any disruption, inefficiency, or inability to retain or expand this distributor base could result in market share loss and adversely affect its business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company, its group company, and promoters are involved in certain ongoing legal proceedings, including criminal and tax-related matters. Any adverse judgments in any of these cases could be detrimental to the company’s business prospects.

The company’s business is impacted by seasonality, with higher demand for products such as water purifiers, water softeners, and fans during the summer months. Any inability to address this fluctuation in demand could adversely affect its business and financial condition.

As of September 30, 2024, the company had trade receivables amounting to Rs 113.52 crore, a sharp increase from Rs 87.65 crore in FY24. Any failure to collect these receivables on time or at all can negatively impact the business and its financial condition.

ipos.name: VLCC
ipos.about: VLCC is a leading Wellness & Beauty brand, offering a comprehensive range of services and products. Founded in 1989 by Mrs. Vandana Luthra, VLCC has grown to operate across 350+ locations in 165 cities and 14 countries. They offer wellness and weight management solutions, beauty treatments, and a wide array of skin, hair, and body care products.

ipos.name: PharmEasy
ipos.about: PharmEasy is a consumer healthcare “super app” that provides consumers with on-demand, home delivered access to a wide range of prescription, OTC pharmaceuticals.

ipos.name: Servify
ipos.about: Servify is a Mumbai-based company that operates as a product lifecycle management platform, focused on after-sales services for devices. It connects brands, retailers, and consumers on a single platform to provide post-purchase support, including warranty and protection plans, device diagnosis, and exchange programs.

ipos.name: Hero Future Energies
ipos.about: Hero Future Energies (HFE), established in 2012, is a renewable energy company focused on providing sustainable and clean energy solutions globally, with a portfolio of wind and solar assets and ventures into green hydrogen production.

ipos.name: Flipkart
ipos.about: Flipkart, an Indian e-commerce giant founded in 2007 by Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal, started as an online bookstore and has expanded to a wide range of products, including electronics, fashion, and home essentials, with a customer base of over 500 million.
strengths: Diverse Product Categories: Flipkart offers a wide range of products, including electronics, fashion, home essentials, groceries, and more.
Customer-Centric Approach: Flipkart is known for its customer-centric innovations, such as Cash on Delivery, No Cost EMI, and easy returns.
Technology Focus: Flipkart invests in technology innovations to improve the customer experience and efficiency of its operations.
risks: Intense Competition: The e-commerce landscape is highly competitive, with Flipkart facing strong competition from other players like Amazon.
Regulatory Challenges: Changes in e-commerce regulations, data protection laws, and taxation policies can pose challenges to Flipkart's operations.
Economic Downturns: Economic downturns or fluctuations in consumer spending can negatively impact e-commerce sales and Flipkart's performance.

ipos.name: PhonePe
ipos.about:
PhonePe Limited is a technology company that builds digital platforms for Payments services, Digital Distribution Services, and Financial Services. Through its flagship PhonePe Platform, it offers Consumer Payments, Merchant Payments, and both Lending and Insurance Distribution services. The company has also expanded into new platforms, including Share.Market, a stock broking and mutual funds distribution platform, and Indus Appstore, a mobile app marketplace. These platforms are built on a proprietary technology stack designed for reliability, scalability, and security.
The company's operations are primarily India-focused, with merchants present across 98.61% of the country's pin codes. It has extended its UPI payments service to ten international markets, including Singapore, UAE, and France, enabling Indian users to make payments when they travel abroad. A significant portion of its user base, 65.22%, comes from Tier-2+ cities.
strengths: The company is the market leader in India's digital payments ecosystem, holding a 49.15% market share of UPI TPV for customer-initiated transactions as of September 2025. This market leadership has been sustained for 58 consecutive months and has translated into strong financial growth, with Total Payment Value (TPV) on its platform growing from ₹69.55 lakh Crores in FY23 to ₹132.70 lakh Crores in FY25.

PhonePe has demonstrated rapid revenue growth and strategic diversification, with revenue from operations growing at a CAGR of 56.25% from ₹2,914.29 Crores in FY23 to ₹7,114.86 Crores in FY25. This growth is supported by a successful diversification strategy, which saw the revenue contribution from Merchant Payments increase from 14.75% to 27.99% and from Lending & Insurance services from 0.96% to 7.84% over the same period.

The company possesses a massive and deeply engaged user base, with 65.76 Crore life-till-date registered users and 4.72 Crore merchants as of September 2025. This scale is reflected in its customer activity metrics, which show a 31.48% CAGR in Daily Active Customers from FY23 to FY25, indicating strong platform stickiness and growing user engagement.

PhonePe has shown significant improvement in profitability, with its restated loss narrowing from ₹2,796.07 Crores in FY23 to ₹1,727.41 Crores in FY25. More significantly, key operational metrics have turned positive, with the company achieving an Adjusted EBITDA of ₹1,477.19 Crores and generating free cash of ₹190.48 Crores in FY25, indicating a strong path towards sustainable profitability.

The company operates a proprietary, in-house technology stack and self-managed infrastructure, a key differentiator in the commoditized payments market. It has invested ₹3,373 Crores in this infrastructure since 2016, which enables greater control over reliability, scalability, security, and cost-efficiency while ensuring 100% data residency in India.

The company has built a highly trusted brand, demonstrated by being India's most downloaded Android finance app with the highest Daily Active Users of 15.6 Crores in H1FY26. This brand trust translates into strong customer retention, with 99.23% of daily customers returning to the platform within 30 days as of September 2025.

The company is successfully executing its diversification strategy into new high-growth areas like wealth management and app distribution. Its Share.Market platform has already opened 1.26 million demat accounts and manages an AUM of ₹5,838 Crores, while its Indus Appstore has secured partnerships with major OEMs like Xiaomi and Motorola to be pre-installed on their smartphones.

PhonePe is backed by strong promoters, WM Digital Commerce Holdings Pte. Ltd. and Wal-Mart International Holdings, Inc., part of the Walmart group. WM Digital holds 71.77% of the pre-offer equity, providing significant financial backing, strategic oversight, and robust corporate governance standards.
risks: The company has a history of significant net losses, recording a loss of ₹1,727.41 Crores in FY25 and ₹1,996.17 Crores in FY24. While losses are narrowing, the company also reported negative cash flows from operating activities of ₹117.27 Crores for the six months ended September 30, 2025, indicating continued cash burn to fund operations and growth.

The business is heavily dependent on its payment services, which accounted for 86.92% of its revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2025, down from 97.66% in FY23. Any downturn in customer willingness to use these services, regulatory changes, or increased competition could materially impact its financial results.

A significant regulatory risk arises from the NPCI's proposed 30% volume cap on UPI transactions for any single Third-Party App Provider (TPAP), which has been deferred until December 31, 2026. With a UPI volume market share of 46.85% as of September 2025, enforcement of this cap could severely impact the company's ability to onboard new users and its overall growth trajectory.

The company's operations are critically dependent on its three sponsor Payment System Provider (PSP) banks: Yes Bank, Axis Bank, and ICICI Bank. Any disruption, failure, change in commercial terms, or operational breakdown with these banks could adversely affect business, as exemplified by the temporary stoppage of its UPI services during the Yes Bank moratorium in March 2020.

The company faces rising payment processing charges, which as a percentage of total expenses, increased from 11.29% in FY23 to 17.97% in FY25. Any significant future increase in these charges by financial institutions, if unable to be passed on to merchants or consumers, could decrease margins and profitability.

The company and its directors are involved in material pending litigations, including 10 tax proceedings against the company with an aggregate amount of ₹24.95 Crores. An adverse outcome in these or other legal matters could lead to significant financial liabilities and reputational damage.

As a large digital platform processing vast amounts of sensitive user data, the company is vulnerable to cybersecurity risks. The recent implementation of India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act introduces significant compliance obligations and potential penalties of up to ₹250 Crores for data breaches, heightening the financial and reputational risk.

ipos.name: FabIndia
ipos.about:
Fabindia is an Indian chain store retailing garments, furnishings, fabrics, and ethnic products handmade by craftspeople across rural India. Fabindia is a legacy brand focusing on handcrafted, indigenous products. The company has established a brand built on artisanal heritage and tradition, inherited across various product categories.
Fabindia links around 50,000 craft-based rural producers to modern urban markets, thereby creating a base for skilled, sustainable rural employment, and preserving India's traditional handicrafts in the process.
strengths: Leading consumer lifestyle brand focused on authentic craft-based products made using sustainable materials & practices
Targets people who desire high-quality Indian lifestyle and organic products
Sustainable  business model which prioritizes the interests of Supplier Community
Established supplier network and supply chain infrastructure
Offers products through multiple channels for seamless customer experience
Managed by a highly experienced team of professionals led by the founder
Capital efficient business model (good investment to expense ratio), with a track record of delivering growth and return on capital
risks: Growth of online retailers may create pricing pressures, increase competition, and adversely affect business, results of operations and financial condition.
Significant dependence on a network of Contract Manufacturers (who in turn engage artisans) and farmers for the manufacture of products.
Significant portion of revenues is dependent on the sale of clothing.
Sale of certain products affected due to seasonal changes.
Outstanding litigation proceedings against Company, Directors, Promoters and Subsidiaries.
Some part of revenue comes from sales at retail franchise stores, failure to maintain such franchise relationships may affect sales, profits.
Focus on using sustainable materials and environmentally processes may lead to increase in the cost of revenue and hinder growth.
Dependent on third-party transportation providers for the delivery of raw materials and products.
Have certain contingent liabilities that have not been provided for in financial statements. If they materialise, they may adversely affect the financial condition.
Have had net outflows of cash from operating activities in the past and may continue to have net cash outflows in future.

ipos.name: OYO
ipos.about: OYO is a leading, new-age technology platform empowering the large yet highly fragmented global hospitality ecosystem. It has been focusing on the short-stay accommodation space since 2012. Its unique business model helps its patrons transform fragmented, unbranded, and underutilized hospitality assets into branded, digitally-enabled storefronts with higher revenue generation potential. OYO provides its customers with high-quality storefronts at compelling price points.
strengths: Largest footprint in terms of hotel storefronts in India and SEA
Second largest footprint in Europe in terms of home storefronts among full stack short-stay accommodation players, according to RedSeer.
Asset-light business model and a lean cost structure - the company does not own the storefronts listed on its platform
Full-stack technology platform
Two flagship Patron applications - Co-OYO and OYO OS
An increase in Patron satisfaction score from 30.1% for the three months ended September 30, 2020 to 72.3% for the three months ended March 31, 2021
Unit economics, measured based on Contribution Profit, has improved from 5.1% in Fiscal 2020 to 18.4% in Fiscal 2021
The proportion of hotel and home storefronts with minimum guarantees or fixed payout commitments from the company has decreased from 14.7% in Fiscal 2019 to 0.1% in Fiscal 2021.
risks: Impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on the travel industry.
Negative cash flows from operating activities in prior years.
Company has incurred net losses in each year since incorporation.
A substantial amount of debt in the past
No control over or ability to predict the actions of our patrons, customers and other third parties, such as neighbors or invitees, during a customer’s stay
Any adverse outcome in legal proceedings involving Zostel may affect the business.
The company is currently involved in a matter before the Competition Commission of India.
There is a pending litigation against the company, certain subsidiaries and directors and promoters.

ipos.name: boAt
ipos.about: Imagine Marketing (boAt) is a digital-first consumer products company and one of the largest Indian digital-first brands in terms of revenue from operations for the financial year 2021. It was founded in 2013 and is led by its flagship brand “boAt” which was launched in 2014. It has products in various segments. It provides audio wearables such as wired headphones and earphones, wireless headphones and earphones (neckbands), bluetooth speakers, home theatre systems among others. It also consists of smartwatches, gaming accessories that include wired and wireless headsets, mouse and keyboards, mobile accessories and personal care appliances.
strengths: One of the largest Indian digital-first brands with leading market positions across multiple fast-growing product categories.
Company’s flagship brand “boAt” is a consumer brand with strong market positioning and a clear value proposition.
Digital-first platform capabilities are targeted to enable growth and continue to allow building a presence across multiple consumer categories.
RedGear brand to cater to the gaming headsets and controllers (keyboard, mouse, mouse pad, joystick) market.
Some products including Rockerz 255, Airdopes 131 and storm smartwatch have a rating of over 4 (out of 5) with over 400,000 ratings across online marketplaces.
In January 2022, the company announced a partnership with Dixon Technologies for manufacturing “Made-in-India” wireless audio devices.
risks: Strength of the company’s flagship “boAt” brand and other brands is crucial to success.
Failure to successfully identify and respond to changing customer preferences and market developments in a cost-effective and timely manner.
Operates in a highly competitive industry including large and established competitors.
Dependence on a number of third-party contract manufacturers and component suppliers for the production of its products.
Risks associated with overseas procurement, such as geographical concentration and foreign currency exchange risks.
Disruptions in its relationships with certain online marketplaces and offline distributors.
Dependence on the audio and wearables category.
Inability to adequately protect its flagship brand ‘boAt’ and its intellectual property.

ipos.name: Bajaj Energy
ipos.about:
Bajaj Energy Ltd. (BEL) and Lalitpur Power Generation Company Ltd. (LPGCL) are among the largest private-sector thermal generation companies in Uttar Pradesh. The company develops, finances and operates thermal power plants in India.
BEL has 450 megawatt coal-based thermal Power plants across 5 locations in Uttar Pradesh.
Bajaj Energy's total gross installed capacity is 2,430 MW. This comprises 450 mega-watts from 5 plants, owned and managed by BEL (the "BEL Power Plants"), and 1,980 MW from
the power plant owned and operated by LPGCL (the "LPGCL Power Plant").
BEL intends to acquire LPGCL completely in future using the proceeds it receives from the IPO offer.
strengths: One of the largest independent power producers in Uttar Pradesh.
Principal fuel supplier is Central Coal Fields Ltd., a subsidiary of Coal India Ltd.
Well-positioned in Uttar Pradesh to capitalise on the state's demand.
All assets are based in Uttar Pradesh. Uttar Pradesh is one of the largest and most densely populated states in India.
Operational power plants have a gross capacity of 2,430 MW. This according to the draft red herring prospectus published in 2019.
risks: Most of the income is derived from electricity sales to one customer: Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. (UPPCL).
As per DRHP, LPGCL is involved in disputes with UPPCL for tariff payment.
Has not been compliant with certain loan agreements in the past resulting in default
Faces fuel supply risks despite having entered into long-term agreements. BEL primarily relies on coal sourced from subsidiaries of Coal India.
Operations carry risk of environmental damage.
Unavailability of appropriate infrastructure could impact the delivery of coal. Heavy dependence on railway infrastructure and road infra for coal.
Tariffs subject to regulatory scrutiny by the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (UPERC)
As per DRHP, the final tariff for LPGCL has not been approved by UPERC.
Majority of the land are under lease agreements and inability to renew the agreement or termination of the agreement could impact revenue and operations.
Financial results subject to seasonal variations.
Operations could be affected by strikes or increased wage demands by the employees.

ipos.name: Arohan Financial
ipos.about: Arohan Financial Services Limited is a leading NBFC-MFI (micro-finance institution) with operations in financially under-penetrated low income states of India. It provides income-generating loans and other financial inclusion-related products to customers who have limited or no access to financial services. It offers a broad range of products to financially underserved customers. The financial products are classified into credit and insurance products.
strengths: Largest NBFC-MFI in Eastern India and fifth largest NBFC-MFI in India with a focus on the low-income states.
Seasoned business model incorporating its well-established risk management framework, loan approval processes, and recovery drives.
Customer-centric approach with diverse product offerings.
Advanced and scalable technology-enabled infrastructure.
Diverse borrowing relationships and access to multiple sources of capital.
Management consists of professionals who have experience in microfinance, consumer finance, investment banking, retail banking, consulting, and insurance.
risks: Inability to control the level of non-performing assets in the future, or its impairment of financial instruments allowance is insufficient to cover future loan losses.
Any disruption in its funding sources.
Vulnerability to interest rate risk and an inability to manage the same.
Asset-liability mismatches that could expose it to interest rate and liquidity risks
Any failure in its IT systems.
Geographic concentration in low-income states like West Bengal, Bihar, Assam, and Odisha.
Inability to maintain its capital adequacy ratio.
Any downgrade in its credit ratings resulting in an increase in its finance costs.
Any changes in laws and regulations applicable to Non-Banking Finance Companies (NBFCs).
Highly competitive industry – the financing industry.
Operational risks including fraud, petty theft, embezzlement, or other misconduct since it deals with large volumes of cash.
Inability to measure or verify customer credit-worthiness or repayment ability data and information.
Exposure to credit, market, and liquidity risks including in respect of its residual MSME lending business.
Inability to develop or implement effective risk management frameworks.
Inability to protect or use its intellectual property rights.
Failure to detect money-laundering and other illegal or improper activities fully or on a timely basis.

ipos.name: Droom
ipos.about: Droom is a technology and data science company that facilitates automobile buying and selling online through a combination of its e-commerce platform along with a technology-driven vertically integrated proprietary ecosystem of products and services for the automobile industry. The company’s automobile e-commerce platform, which includes website and mobile apps, offers the facility to buy and sell new and used vehicles. Some of the elements of automobile buying covered on the company’s platforms are searching for a vehicle, creating buying requirements, price discovery, booking, certification to purchase and financing and doorstep delivery.
strengths: End-to-end e-commerce platform for buying and selling used vehicles in India.
Purely online player which allows the company to escape expensive real estate, and high cost of capital.
An asset-light and technology-driven platform.
As of September 30, 2021, the company had over 278,807 used vehicles listed across 11 categories present across 1,151 cities in India.
As of September 30, 2021, the company had 14.46 million cumulative downloads of its mobile app.
The company holds a valid patent in the United States for Orange Book Value (OBV), its used vehicle pricing solution.
Other platforms such as its AI-based vehicle inspection service and Droom Credit, an automobile-focused lending platform have been developed entirely in-house.
The number of auto dealers on its platform has increased at a CAGR of 11.57% from 16,175 as of March 31, 2019, to 20,133 as of March 31, 2021, and were 20,725 as of September 30, 2021.
risks: Business heavily reliant on India’s used and new automobile and vehicular services e-commerce industry - any impact on the overall market will likely have an impact on the company’s business.
Inability to add more auto dealers or a reduction in the number of auto dealers on the platform could have a material adverse effect on the business.
There are outstanding legal proceedings involving the company, its directors, promoter, and subsidiaries.

The company intends to utilise a certain amount from the net proceeds of the IPO towards potential acquisitions and strategic initiatives - if there is any shortfall the company may raise requisite capital through means such as internal accruals and/or seeking debt.
Funding requirements are based on internal management estimates and its current business plans have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
Demand for used vehicles is subject to seasonal fluctuations.
Limited number of third-party financing partners to fund loans facilitated through its platform
Negative cash flows from operating activities in the three months ended June 30, 2021, and Fiscals 2021, 2020, and 2019.

ipos.name: Crystal Crop Protection
ipos.about:
Crystal Crop Protection Limited is an agrochemical and seed company established in 1994. The company develops, manufactures, and distributes crop protection products, natural crop solutions, technical-grade active ingredients, and seeds. Its crop protection portfolio includes herbicides, fungicides, insecticides, bio-stimulants, bio-protectants, plant growth regulators, liquid fertilisers, and micronutrients. 
Its seed portfolio covers field crops such as cotton, mustard, maize, rice, and wheat, along with vegetable and flower seeds. The company also manufactures self-propelled boom sprayers and sells conventional sprayers. It operates four formulation manufacturing units in Haryana, Gujarat, and Jammu and two technical manufacturing units in Gujarat and Maharashtra. 
Its seed processing facilities are located in Hyderabad, Telangana, and Bengaluru, Karnataka. The company also operates research and development facilities across multiple states, including its Key Research and Development Centre in Sonipat, Haryana.
strengths: The company claims to have dedicated R&D facilities for crop protection products and seeds, including its Key Research Development Centre (KRDC) in Sonipat, Haryana, which is recognised by the Department of Science and Technology and has received GLP compliance certification. As of the date of the prospectus, it had applied for 28 patents, of which 18 were granted in India and two outside India. It also had 14 patents commercialised as of March 31, 2026.

As of June 30, 2026, the company had 139 domestic registrations for technical-grade products, 601 domestic formulation registrations and 147 export registrations for technicals and formulations. Its seed portfolio comprised over 275 hybrid varieties, including 111 field crop varieties, 139 vegetable seed varieties, and 25 marigold varieties. It also held 63 plant variety protection (PVP) registrations across cotton, pearl millet, sorghum, and mustard.

The company has entered into product development and technology collaborations with multinational companies such as Bayer, BASF, Corteva, Cibus, and Traitomic. These arrangements cover crop protection formulations, herbicide-tolerant mustard varieties, insect-resistant cotton seeds, and gene-editing research in mustard. It has also collaborated with the World Vegetable Centre on developing disease-resistant okra varieties.

The company has acquired several established agrochemical brands, including Bavistin from BASF; Proclaim, Tilt, and Blue Copper from Syngenta; Dursban and Nurelle D from Dow AgroSciences; and Gramoxone from Syngenta. Its seed business has also expanded through acquisitions from Bayer, Syngenta, Kohinoor Seeds, and I&B Seeds. These acquisitions have added established products and brands to its existing portfolio.

The company claims to operate four crop protection formulation manufacturing units with an aggregate installed capacity of 75,962 MT and two technical-grade manufacturing units with a combined capacity of 4,717 MT as of June 30, 2026. It also operates three seed processing units with a combined installed capacity of 49,935.79 MT. Its formulation manufacturing units are accredited with ISO 9001:2015 quality management and ISO 14001:2015 environmental management system standards.

As of June 30, 2026, the company had a distribution network of 14,717 independent distributors across 23 states and four union territories. Its network also included 34 distribution centres and three regional distribution centres. The company had 729 employees supporting its crop protection sales network and 489 employees supporting its seeds business.

The company’s portfolio covers crop protection products, natural crop solutions, technical-grade active ingredients, and hybrid seeds across field crops, vegetables, and flowers. It also exports crop protection products and seeds to multiple international markets. As of June 30, 2026, it held 53 product registrations across 14 overseas jurisdictions, including Europe and Brazil.
risks: The company, its promoters, and one of its directors are subject to ongoing criminal and regulatory proceedings relating to alleged violations of the Foreign Trade Policy (2009–2014) and the Handbook of Procedures of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade. Any adverse outcome in these proceedings could negatively affect the company’s business, financial condition, cash flows, and reputation.

A significant portion of the company’s revenue from operations is derived from its domestic business in India. Domestic sales contributed Rs 1,160.05 crore (96.90%), Rs 3,006.38 crore (95.38%), Rs 2,622.64 crore (97.48%), and Rs 2,180.76 crore (97.80%) to revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026, FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Further, crop protection products and natural crop solutions contributed Rs 793.34 crore (63.20%), Rs 2,476.56 crore (80.42%), Rs 2,201.01 crore (81.74%) and Rs 1,836.72 crore (83.40%) during the same periods. Any adverse changes in the Indian crop protection and natural crop solutions industry, a decline in domestic demand, or failure to introduce new products in response to changing regulatory and market requirements could negatively affect the company’s business and financial condition.

The company’s business is exposed to climatic conditions, pest attacks and seasonal variations in agricultural activity. Adverse weather conditions, including droughts, floods, unseasonal rainfall and heat waves, can affect crop yields, sowing patterns, pest incidence and farmers’ demand for crop protection products, natural crop solutions and seeds. The company’s sales, inventory requirements, capacity utilisation and working capital needs are also dependent on Kharif and Rabi cropping seasons, and any mismatch between inventory build-up and actual demand could result in higher holding costs, product obsolescence, stock-outs and lower margins. Any adverse changes in weather conditions, pest outbreaks or cropping patterns could negatively affect the company’s business, cash flows and financial performance.

The company, its subsidiaries, promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, and senior management personnel are involved in various ongoing legal proceedings amounting to Rs 341.95 crore as of June 30, 2026, representing 16.76% of the company’s net worth. Any adverse judgments or penalties in these proceedings could result in additional payments, higher expenses, and increased current or contingent liabilities, adversely affecting the company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.

The company’s crop protection and seeds businesses require significant investment in research and development, while new products may take 5–7 years to reach the market due to stringent testing and regulatory approval requirements. Any failure to develop commercially viable products, obtain timely registrations or respond to technological advancements and changing customer preferences could result in delays, higher costs, or loss of market share to competitors, adversely affecting the company’s business and cash flows.

The company recorded negative cash flows from investing activities amounting to Rs 90.69 crore, Rs 215.90 crore, Rs 673.43 crore, and Rs 229.71 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. These outflows primarily arose from purchases of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and investments, along with payments towards asset and business acquisitions. The company also recorded negative cash flows from financing activities amounting to Rs 95.10 crore in FY24, mainly due to repayments of current and non-current borrowings, dividend payments, lease liabilities, and finance costs, partially offset by proceeds from current borrowings. Sustained outflows could adversely affect its liquidity, working capital requirements, and financial condition.

The company had trade receivables of Rs 810.66 crore as of June 30, 2026, indicating a significant amount of funds outstanding from its customers. Any delay or failure in recovering these receivables could adversely affect the company’s cash flows, working capital position, and financial condition.

As of August 31, 2026, the company and its subsidiaries had consolidated outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 974.51 crore. Any difficulty in servicing or refinancing these borrowings could adversely affect the company’s cash flows, financial condition, and results of operations.

ipos.name: Antala Industries
ipos.about:
Antala Industries Limited is engaged in the manufacturing, processing, printing, laminating and supply of industrial and commercial packaging products. The company's product portfolio includes Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene (BOPP) bags, BOPP printing rolls, BOPP lamination rolls, polypropylene (PP) woven bags, and PP woven lamination rolls.
The company supplies packaging products to industries such as food processing, fertilisers, chemicals, cement, construction, textiles, and seeds. Its products are available in different sizes, capacities, and specifications, with customisation options for printing, lamination, and finishing.
The company operates a manufacturing facility in Rajkot, Gujarat, equipped with machinery for extrusion lamination, rotogravure printing, multicolour printing, cutting, stitching, and finishing. The facility supports various stages of production, from printing and lamination to the packaging of finished products.
The company was originally established as a partnership firm under the name M/s Octagon Industries on April 30, 2021, and was subsequently converted into a public limited company under the name Antala Industries Limited on August 5, 2024.

Use of proceeds: 
The IPO is a fresh issue of shares. The proceeds from the issue will be used for the following purposes:
To meet working capital requirements - Rs 10.68 crore
To meet the requirements of capital expenditure towards purchase of machinery -Rs 5.89 crore
General corporate purposes
strengths: Antala Industries is engaged in the manufacture of five categories of packaging products, including BOPP bags, BOPP printing rolls, BOPP lamination rolls, PP woven bags, and PP woven lamination rolls. It caters to industries such as cement, chemicals, fertilisers, FMCG, and textiles.

The company has seen a consistent increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). The revenue from operations increased from Rs 12.51 crore in FY24 to Rs 31.85 crore in FY25 and Rs 47.40 crore in FY26. Its profit after tax (PAT) also increased from Rs 0.88 crore to Rs 1.82 crore and Rs 4.24 crore during the same periods, respectively.

The company has reported an increase in capacity utilisation across its manufacturing operations. Printing machinery utilisation increased from 20.07% in FY24 to 51.26% in FY25 to 76.05% in FY26, while lamination machinery utilisation rose from 20.23% to 51.68% to 76.67% during the same period. The company's printing machinery installed capacity increased from 330 lakh metres per annum in FY24 to 370.63 lakh metres per annum to 442.50 lakh metres per annum in FY26, while the capacity utilisation during the same period stood at 66.23 lakh metres per annum, 189.98 lakh metres per annum, and 336.50 lakh metres per annum.

The company claims to have an integrated manufacturing facility in Rajkot, Gujarat, equipped with an eight-colour rotogravure printing machine, a flexographic printing machine, automated cutting machinery, and bag conversion lines. The facility supports multiple stages of packaging production.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for quality management systems, ISO 14001:2015 for environmental management systems, ISO 45001:2018 for occupational health and safety management systems, and ISO 22000:2018 for food safety management systems.

The company's revenue concentration among its top 10 customers declined from 94.28% (Rs 11.80 crore) in FY24 to 47.43% (Rs 22.48 crore) in FY26. This indicates a more diversified customer base, reducing its dependence on a limited number of customers and the potential impact of losing any major customer on its revenue.
risks: Despite a decline in customer concentration over the years, Antala Industries continues to derive a significant portion of its revenue from its top 10 customers. These customers contributed Rs 11.80 crore (94.28%) in FY24, Rs 14.93 crore (46.87%) in FY25, and Rs 22.48 crore (47.43%) in FY26 to its revenue from operations, respectively. The loss of major customers or a reduction in their orders could adversely affect the company's revenue and profitability.

The company's revenue is geographically concentrated in Gujarat, which accounted for Rs 12.45 crore (99.49%), Rs 25.55 crore (80.22%), and Rs 33.70 crore (71.08%) of its revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Any adverse economic, regulatory or operational developments in the state could significantly affect the company's business and financial performance.

The company depends heavily on Gujarat for raw material procurement. Purchases from the state amounted to Rs 10.73 crore (99.97%), Rs 25.71 crore (96.59%), and Rs 38.66 crore (91.80%) of total raw material purchases in FY24, FY25 and FY26, respectively. Any disruption in regional supply chains could affect production schedules and increase procurement costs.

The company recorded negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 3.28 crore in FY25 and Rs 4.88 crore in FY26, primarily due to increases in inventories, trade receivables, and short-term loans and advances. It also recorded negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 0.03 crore, Rs 0.49 crore, and Rs 1.78 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, and negative cash flow from financing activities of Rs 0.10 crore in FY24. Sustained cash outflows could affect the company's liquidity and ability to meet its operational and financial obligations.

The company operates its manufacturing activities from a single facility in Rajkot, Gujarat, situated on rented premises under a seven-year agreement beginning June 1, 2026. Any disruption at this facility or termination of the lease could interrupt production, affect order fulfilment, and result in additional relocation expenses.
