The company has experienced delays in complying with statutory filing requirements under the Companies Act, 2013, including delays of up to 294 days in filing certain forms. It has also filed applications for adjudication concerning procedural non-compliances, which could result in penalties, additional regulatory obligations, or increased scrutiny.

The company's manufacturing operations depend on petroleum-derived raw materials, including polypropylene granules, LDPE granules, and BOPP films. Fluctuations in petrochemical prices, environmental restrictions on plastic-based packaging, or a shift towards alternative packaging materials could increase costs and reduce demand for its products.
As of September 30, 2026, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 1.75 crore. Any failure to service or repay these loans can harm the company’s operations and financial position.

Antala Industries derived 63.14% of its revenue from repeat customers in FY26, compared to 39.46% in FY25. For the six months ended September 30, 2026, repeat customers contributed 85.34% of its revenue. Since customer arrangements are generally based on purchase orders without guaranteed future business, the loss of repeat customers or a reduction in their orders could adversely affect the company's revenue, profitability and capacity utilisation.

ipos.name: Vedant Poly Fabs Solutions
ipos.about:
Vedant Poly Fabs Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of flexible packaging materials and supplies to business-to-business (B2B) customers across India. Its product portfolio includes 3-layer and 5-layer low-density (LD) films, shrink films, barrier films, printed laminates, and milk and oil pouches used in food and beverage and other consumer product packaging. 
The company manufactures products according to customer specifications, including size, thickness, material composition, and printing requirements. Its manufacturing processes include extrusion, printing, lamination, slitting, and pouching. The facility is equipped with multilayer extrusion machines, central impression (CI) flexographic printing machines, and rotogravure printing machines. 
In addition to manufacturing, the company trades in billet strips used in engineering, fabrication, and manufacturing industries. It commenced operations in 2018 and expanded its manufacturing capacity in March 2026 by adding lamination, slitting, and pouching machines. The company also operates a reprocessing unit to process plastic waste generated during manufacturing for reuse in certain applications.
strengths: The company undertakes extrusion, printing, lamination, slitting, and rewinding at its in-house manufacturing facility. This allows it to manage multiple production stages within a single facility.

The company claims to have an in-house laboratory equipped with testing instruments, including a dart impact tester, coefficient of friction (COF) tester, and universal testing machine. These instruments are used to evaluate film impact resistance, surface characteristics, sealing strength, and tensile strength.

The company’s lamination production increased from 73,648.33 kg in FY24 to 13,60,511.10 kg in FY25 and 30,82,044.37 kg in FY26. This reflects an increase in production volume over the three financial years.

The company manufactures multilayer LD films, printed plastics, milk films, shrink films, printed laminates, and aluminium foil laminates. It added milk and oil printed plastic rolls and printed laminates in 2023, followed by aluminium foil laminates in 2024.

The company claims to operate its own fleet of eight vehicles for delivering finished goods to customers. This allows it to coordinate dispatch schedules internally and reduces its reliance on third-party transportation providers.

The company’s manufacturing facility is located in Barasat, West Bengal, with access to road and rail networks. According to the prospectus, its proximity to certain raw material suppliers and markets in eastern India supports procurement and product distribution.

The company has witnessed a consistent increase in its revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 49.53 crore in FY24 to Rs 81.02 crore in FY25 and Rs 115.14 crore in FY26. PAT increased from Rs 0.63 crore in FY24 to Rs 4.56 crore in FY25 and Rs 10.97 crore in FY26.
risks: The company is dependent on its suppliers for the uninterrupted supply of raw materials, and its top 10 suppliers contributed Rs 88.28 crore (90.16%), Rs 41.35 crore (53.24%), and Rs 16.80 crore (35.13%) of total purchases in FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any disruption in raw material supplies or increase in raw material and other input costs due to price volatility, currency fluctuations, or changes in government policies could adversely affect the company’s production, product pricing, and financial performance.

The company’s top 10 customers contributed Rs 79.95 crore (69.44%), Rs 24.43 crore (30.15%), and Rs 6.68 crore (13.49%) of total sales in FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any loss of these key customers, reduction in orders, or inability to replace lost business in a timely manner could adversely affect the company’s revenue, cash flows, and financial performance.

The company generally receives customer orders through verbal communications and does not typically obtain formal written purchase orders or long-term contracts. Miscommunication about product specifications, quantities, printing requirements, or delivery schedules could cause order discrepancies, delays, additional costs, and customer disputes, adversely affecting the company’s business and financial performance.

The company generated Rs 111.45 crore (96.80%), Rs 79.32 crore (97.90%), and Rs 48.86 crore (98.64%) of its revenue from West Bengal in FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any adverse political or geographical developments, increased competition, or changes in customer demand in the state could affect the company’s ability to retain customers and adversely impact its revenue and profitability.

The company reported negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 11.46 crore, Rs 5.74 crore, and Rs 3.45 crore in FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively, primarily due to decreases in trade payables and other current liabilities, increases in trade receivables, inventories, and other current assets, and an increase in short-term loans and advances. It also reported negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 28.65 crore, Rs 6.66 crore, and Rs 2.51 crore in the same periods, mainly due to purchases of fixed assets and increases in non-current investments. The company’s working capital-intensive operations and capital expenditure requirements may continue to strain liquidity if operating cash inflows remain insufficient or the expected returns from new assets do not materialise.

The company, its directors, promoters, promoter group, and group companies are involved in ongoing legal proceedings. Any adverse decisions in these matters could result in financial liabilities, including demand amounts, interest, and penalties, divert management time and attention, and adversely affect the company’s business, results of operations, and financial condition.

The company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 46.81 crore as of March 31, 2026. Any failure to service or repay its borrowings on time could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company had trade receivables of Rs 28.37 crore as of March 31, 2026. Any delay or failure in collecting these receivables could increase working capital requirements and adversely affect the company’s cash flows and financial condition.

ipos.name: Vectras Enprocon
ipos.about:
Vectras Enprocon Limited is a Gujarat-based engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company operating in the midstream and downstream segments of the oil and gas industry. Incorporated in May 2021, the company undertakes pipeline construction, combined oil and gas station works, and associated infrastructure projects across various states in India.
Its services include design, engineering, procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning of cross-country pipelines, spur pipelines, city gas distribution networks, oil and gas terminals, and stations. The company also undertakes mechanical, electrical, and civil works at refineries, petrochemical complexes, gas processing units, and petroleum depots.
Additionally, Vectras Enprocon provides civil infrastructure services, including site development, road construction, foundations, and drainage systems. Its other services include electrical and instrumentation works, cathodic protection, pipeline inspection, pressure testing, and safety auditing.
The company is headquartered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and serves both public sector undertakings and private sector companies.
strengths: As of September 30, 2026, Vectras Enprocon had an unexecuted order book of Rs 183.28 crore comprising 34 projects, with a book-to-bill ratio of 2.55 times, providing visibility for future growth. Combined oil and gas station works accounted for Rs 116.29 crore (63.45%) of the order book, followed by pipeline works at Rs 59.46 crore (32.44%) and other allied services at Rs 7.53 crore (4.11%).

The company has completed certain projects ahead of their scheduled completion dates. According to the RHP, the company completed one public sector project 160 days ahead of schedule in FY23, while a private sector project was completed 62 days early in FY24.

The company has expanded its geographical presence beyond Gujarat. As of September 30, 2026, Gujarat accounted for Rs 112.90 crore (61.60%) of its order book, followed by Chhattisgarh at Rs 26.38 crore (14.40%), Maharashtra at Rs 21.57 crore (11.77%), Bihar at Rs 9.33 crore (5.09%) and Punjab at Rs 6.52 crore (3.55%). This geographical diversification could help the company access a wider range of project opportunities and reduce its dependence on a single state.

The company has seen an increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 54.32 crore in FY24 to Rs 80.48 crore in FY25 and Rs 119.80 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 5.81 crore in FY24 to Rs 10.17 crore in FY25 and Rs 15.43 crore in FY26.

The company claims to have in-house design and operations teams for project planning and execution. As of September 30, 2026, it had 990 permanent employees, including 911 in operations, 21 in quality assurance and control, and 15 in health, safety, and environment.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for Quality Management Systems, ISO 45001:2018 for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems, ISO 14001:2015 for Environmental Management Systems, and ISO 27001:2022 for Information Security Management Systems.
risks: The company depends heavily on a limited number of customers for its revenue. Its top 10 customers contributed Rs 53.14 crore (97.84%), Rs 77.30 crore (96.04%), and Rs 110.54 crore (92.27%) to revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Loss of major customers, reduced orders, or payment delays could adversely affect the company's revenue, cash flows, and profitability.

The company relies on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials and components. Purchases from its top 10 suppliers amounted to Rs 16.93 crore (72.87%) in FY24, Rs 14.45 crore (61.67%) in FY25 and Rs 23.34 crore (68.64%) in FY26. During the six months ended September 30, 2026, these purchases stood at Rs 7.79 crore (45.23%). Any disruption in supplies, quality issues, or an increase in procurement costs could delay project execution and reduce profitability.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from combined oil and gas station works. This segment contributed Rs 46.50 crore (85.59%), Rs 51.36 crore (63.82%), and Rs 45.64 crore (38.09%) to revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Any adverse change in demand for these services, increased competition, or delays in project awards could affect the company's revenue and financial performance.

The company generates a substantial portion of its revenue from Gujarat and Maharashtra. These two states collectively contributed Rs 50.29 crore (92.59%) in FY24, Rs 72.21 crore (89.72%) in FY25, and Rs 85.68 crore (71.52%) in FY26. Any adverse changes in regional economic conditions, government policies, or oil and gas infrastructure investments could affect the company's operations and profitability.

The company reported negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 1.29 crore, Rs 4.44 crore, and Rs 5.10 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively, followed by Rs 3.14 crore during the six months ended September 30, 2026. These outflows were primarily driven by increasing working capital requirements, particularly inventory accumulation, along with changes in receivables, other assets, and liabilities. Sustained negative operating cash flows could increase the company's dependence on external financing and affect its ability to fund ongoing projects and expansion plans.

The company relies on third-party service providers for labour, drilling, and excavation activities. Expenses related to these services amounted to Rs 12.93 crore (23.81% of revenue from operations) in FY24, Rs 33.51 crore (41.64%) in FY25, and Rs 55.10 crore (45.99%) in FY26. Delays, labour shortages, or deficiencies in services provided by these contractors could lead to project delays, cost overruns, and contractual penalties.

The company's net trade receivables stood at Rs 8.86 crore in FY24, Rs 19.05 crore in FY25, and Rs 21.16 crore in FY26. Credit sales have been rising over the years, and any delay or default in collecting payments from customers could affect the company's working capital, cash flows, and financial condition.

As of September 30, 2026, the company had aggregate outstanding borrowings of Rs 31.36 crore, including secured outstanding debt of Rs 22.99 crore. Certain financing agreements impose restrictions on changes in ownership, capital structure, investments, and other business decisions. Any failure to meet repayment obligations or comply with lender conditions could result in enforcement against secured assets and restrict the company's financial and operational flexibility.

The company has reported delays in filing statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, including a 116-day delay in filing Form DPT-3 in FY26 and a 71-day delay in filing Form AOC-4 for FY23. It has also disclosed delays in depositing provident fund, ESIC, and TDS dues, including a 202-day delay in a provident fund deposit relating to July 2024. Any future non-compliance or regulatory penalties could increase costs and adversely affect the company's financial condition.

ipos.name: Maxwell Engineering
ipos.about:
Maxwell Engineering Solutions Limited is a precision engineering company engaged in the manufacturing, trading, and servicing of components used in underwater pelletising systems. The company operates through three business segments: manufacturing, services, and trading.
Its product portfolio includes pelletising die plates, pelletising blades and knives, blade holders, cutter hubs, tapped driving bushes, and other spare components. The company also undertakes customised manufacturing based on customer specifications and supplies products on a white-label basis.
Its services include refurbishment and repair of used die plates, intermediary support, and management consulting. The company also trades complementary components used in pelletising systems. Its products are used in industries such as polymer compounding, masterbatches, engineering plastics, cable compounds, specialty polymers, and plastics recycling.
The company operates a manufacturing facility at Waghodia GIDC in Vadodara, Gujarat, which commenced operations in July 2025. It also serves customers across domestic and international markets.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO is a fresh issue of shares.​ Net proceeds from the issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​
Financing the capital expenditure requirement towards the purchase of new machinery, lab equipment & other utilities for the manufacturing facility — Rs 18 crore
Financing the capital expenditure requirement for construction of new office building and manufacturing facility   — Rs 6.5 crore
Repayment/prepayment, in full or part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by the company — Rs 4.3 crore
Funding working capital requirements of the company — Rs 14 crore
General corporate purposes
strengths: The company has reported consistent growth in revenue from operations, increasing from Rs 10.54 crore in FY24 to Rs 22.10 crore in FY25 and Rs 29.45 crore in FY26. Its profit after tax (PAT) also increased from Rs 3.16 crore in FY24 to Rs 9.17 crore in FY25 and Rs 11.86 crore in FY26.

The company exports its products to more than 25 countries, including Germany, the USA, the Netherlands, Israel, and Austria. Export revenue increased from Rs 8.47 crore in FY24 to Rs 18.22 crore in FY25 and Rs 24.95 crore in FY26. Exports contributed 84.34% of revenue during the four months ended July 31, 2026.

The company manufactures customised components based on customer specifications, including blade holders and cutter hubs with straight, inclined and custom-built designs. It also offers white-label manufacturing, allowing customers to sell products under their own brands. This enables the company to meet different equipment requirements and serve different customer segments.

The company claims to have an in-house R&D unit focused on precision engineering and product development. It undertook development work across nine projects, including oil-heated die plates, carbide-tipped plates, and large-format plates. These capabilities may help the company expand its product range and address specialised customer requirements.

The company claims to have manufacturing equipment, including CNC machines, VMC machines, EDM machines, wire-cut machines, vacuum furnaces, and surface grinding machines. Its company-owned manufacturing facility at Waghodia GIDC, Vadodara, commenced operations in July 2025. The facility may support higher production capacity, reduce reliance on outsourced manufacturing, and improve delivery timelines.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for manufacturing and supplying die plates/heads, pelletising blades/knives, blade holders, and tapped driving bushes. It also received the ZED Bronze Certification under the MSME Sustainable (ZED) Certification Scheme on November 28, 2025. These certifications provide documented recognition of its quality management and sustainable manufacturing practices.

The company operates through manufacturing, trading, and services. In FY26, manufacturing generated Rs 18.50 crore (62.84%), trading contributed Rs 5.33 crore (18.11%), and services accounted for Rs 5.61 crore (19.05%). These segments allow the company to generate revenue from product manufacturing, component trading, and refurbishment services rather than relying on a single activity.
risks: The company depends heavily on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials and traded components. Purchases from its top 10 suppliers amounted to Rs 2.17 crore (86.83%) in FY24, Rs 4.26 crore (89.67%) in FY25 and Rs 6.69 crore (80.22%) in FY26. Their contribution stood at Rs 3.59 crore (87.10%) during the four months ended July 31, 2026. Any disruption in supplies or changes in procurement terms could delay production, affect order fulfilment and reduce profitability.

The company relies on imports for carbide and brazing filler, which are essential to its manufacturing operations. Imported raw material purchases amounted to Rs 0.53 crore (64.59%) in FY24, Rs 0.85 crore (65.30%) in FY25 and Rs 1.64 crore (62.35%) in FY26. Imports stood at Rs 1.18 crore (34.03%) during the four months ended July 31, 2026. Any increase in import duties, foreign exchange fluctuations, or international supply disruptions could increase production costs and affect profit margins.

The company has outstanding export obligations of Rs 13.10 crore under the Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme, to be fulfilled by March 25, 2031. Failure to meet these obligations could result in the recovery of customs duty benefits, along with applicable interest and penalties, adversely affecting its cash flows and financial position.

The company derives a substantial portion of its revenue from exports. Export sales accounted for 80.38% of revenue from operations in FY24, 82.43% in FY25 and 84.73% in FY26, with the contribution standing at 84.34% during the four months ended July 31, 2026. The company does not currently use foreign exchange hedging arrangements, leaving its revenue realisations and profitability exposed to adverse currency movements.

The company depends on a limited number of customers for a significant portion of its revenue. Its top 10 customers contributed Rs 7.43 crore (70.45%) in FY24, Rs 16.14 crore (73.03%) in FY25 and Rs 19.35 crore (65.71%) in FY26. Their contribution stood at Rs 9.58 crore (80.71%) during the four months ended July 31, 2026. The absence of long-term customer agreements increases the risk of order cancellations or reduced business, which could adversely affect revenue and profitability.

The company relies on steel as a major raw material, with purchases amounting to Rs 0.29 crore (34.97% of raw material purchases) in FY24, Rs 0.45 crore (34.28%) in FY25 and Rs 0.99 crore (37.47%) in FY26. Steel purchases increased to Rs 2.28 crore (65.96%) during the four months ended July 31, 2026. Any significant increase in steel prices or disruption in domestic supply could raise production costs and reduce profit margins.

The company's contingent liabilities amounted to Rs 0.30 crore in FY24, Rs 2.48 crore in FY25, and Rs 2.19 crore in FY26. They remained at Rs 2.19 crore as of July 31, 2026, primarily relating to customs duty benefits under the EPCG Scheme. If these liabilities materialise, they could adversely affect the company's financial position and cash flows.

The company has reported delays in statutory filings and payments relating to the Companies Act, EPF, ESIC, and TDS. It has also received an ESIC notice concerning alleged statutory non-compliance. Although no penalties had been imposed as of the RHP date for the reported delays, adverse regulatory action could result in financial penalties, additional compliance costs, and reputational damage.

ipos.name: Johnsoncab Electricals
ipos.about:
Johnsoncab Electricals Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of low-voltage wires and cables with voltage ratings of up to 1.1 kV. The company was originally established as a partnership firm in 2012 and manufactures and sells its products under the brand name ‘Johnson Cables.'
Its product portfolio includes power cables, housing and building wires, industrial single-core and multicore control cables, submersible flat cables, solar and photovoltaic cables, and welding cables. These products are used across sectors such as power generation, transmission and distribution, renewable energy, railways, construction, manufacturing, agriculture and industrial operations.
The company operates two manufacturing units in Mehsana, Gujarat, with a combined annual installed capacity of 79,950 kilometres as of FY26. Its manufacturing processes include wire drawing, annealing, bunching, insulation, extrusion, testing, and packaging. The company serves private sector customers and government entities through direct orders, tenders, and vendor approval processes.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO is a fresh issue of shares. The proceeds from the issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​
Funding the capital expenditure requirements of the company towards 
Construction of additional factory shed for expansion - Rs 7.89 crore
Purchase of additional plant & machinery for increasing the production capacity - Rs 9.38 crore
Purchase of new machinery to manufacture paper-insulated copper/aluminium conductors - Rs 5.72 crore
Purchase and set up a rooftop solar power plant - Rs 3.23 crore
Additional working capital requirement - Rs 14 crore
General corporate purposes
strengths: Johnsoncab Electricals has reported consistent growth in revenue from operations, increasing from Rs 88.34 crore in FY24 to Rs 139.79 crore in FY25 and Rs 210.47 crore in FY26. Its profit after tax (PAT) also increased from Rs 2.52 crore in FY24 to Rs 5.46 crore in FY25 and Rs 13.42 crore in FY26.

The company invested Rs 9.84 crore in FY24, Rs 1.65 crore in FY25, and Rs 16.90 crore in FY26 in plant, machinery, equipment, factory buildings, and sheds. As of March 31, 2026, its two manufacturing units had a combined annual installed capacity of 79,950 kilometres of wires and cables. These investments support increased production capacity and the manufacture of different cable specifications.

The company generates revenue from both private entities and government customers. Revenue from public sector units and state government agencies increased from Rs 4.92 crore (5.57%) in FY24 to Rs 25.98 crore (18.58%) in FY25 and Rs 39.75 crore (18.89%) in FY26. Revenue from private entities stood at Rs 83.41 crore, Rs 113.81 crore, and Rs 170.72 crore, respectively. This provides the company with access to business opportunities across both customer segments.

The company holds Indian Patent No. 420982 for an improved three-core double-insulated flat electrical cable for submersible pumps. The patent was granted on February 8, 2023, and is valid until June 30, 2042, subject to payment of renewal fees. This provides intellectual property protection for a specialised product in its submersible cable portfolio.

The company has vendor registrations and approvals with organisations including Western Railway, Uttar Gujarat Vij Company Limited (UGVCL), Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (JVVNL), Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC), and Gujarat's Roads and Buildings Department. These registrations allow it to participate in eligible tenders for supplying wires and cables, subject to applicable tender requirements.

The company manufactures photovoltaic DC solar cables and aluminium solar earthing wires. Its revenue from the renewable energy sector increased from Rs 18.03 crore (20.41% of revenue from operations) in FY24 to Rs 23.25 crore (16.63%) in FY25 and Rs 48.91 crore (23.24%) in FY26. This provides exposure to demand from renewable energy projects and reduces reliance on traditional cable applications.

The company states that its manufacturing facilities are certified under ISO 9001:2015 for quality management systems, ISO 14001:2015 for environmental management systems and ISO 45001:2018 for occupational health and safety management systems.

Its cost of goods sold (COGS) as a percentage of revenue declined from 90.50% in FY24 to 88.25% in FY25 and 85.12% in FY26. The declining COGS ratio indicates improved cost efficiency, which can support operating margins.
risks: The company does not have long-term agreements with most of its raw material suppliers. Purchases from its top 10 suppliers amounted to Rs 30.00 crore (36.38%) in FY24, Rs 76.54 crore (64.05%) in FY25 and Rs 97.48 crore (49.30%) in FY26. The company also does not hedge against fluctuations in copper, aluminum, and other raw material prices. Any supply disruption or increase in raw material costs that cannot be passed on to customers could affect production, profitability, and cash flows.

The company generates a significant portion of its revenue from a limited number of customers. Its top 10 customers contributed Rs 24.89 crore (28.18%) in FY24, Rs 72.50 crore (51.87%) in FY25 and Rs 139.41 crore (66.24%) in FY26. The company does not have long-term or exclusive arrangements with these customers. The loss of major customers or a reduction in their orders could significantly affect revenue, profitability, and cash flows.

The company generates a substantial portion of its revenue from Gujarat. Revenue from the state amounted to Rs 68.40 crore (77.43%) in FY24, Rs 98.55 crore (70.50%) in FY25, and Rs 149.24 crore (70.91%) in FY26. Any adverse changes in regional demand, infrastructure spending, government policies, or economic conditions could affect the company's sales and profitability.

The company had outstanding borrowings of Rs 79.88 crore as of March 31, 2026, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.54 times. Its high debt obligations could divert cash flows towards interest and principal repayments, restrict additional borrowing, and limit funds available for working capital and expansion. Any inability to service or refinance its borrowings could adversely affect its financial condition and operations.

The company derives a substantial portion of its revenue from the railway and renewable energy sectors. These sectors collectively contributed Rs 22.94 crore (25.97%) in FY24, Rs 49.13 crore (35.15%) in FY25 and Rs 88.64 crore (42.12%) in FY26, based on the disclosed industry-wise figures. Any slowdown in railway projects, renewable energy investments, or related government expenditure could reduce demand for its products and affect revenue and profitability.

The company reported negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 4.26 crore in FY24, Rs 1.73 crore in FY25, and Rs 19.70 crore in FY26. The negative cash flow in FY26 was primarily due to increased working capital requirements arising from business expansion, higher inventories of Rs 26.54 crore and higher trade receivables of Rs 16.03 crore. It also reported negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 9.91 crore, Rs 3.39 crore, and Rs 16.69 crore, respectively. Continued negative operating cash flows could increase dependence on external financing and affect the company's ability to fund operations, repay borrowings and execute expansion plans.

The company's Unit I contributed Rs 88.34 crore (100%) in FY24, Rs 130.36 crore (93.25%) in FY25, and Rs 146.88 crore (69.79%) in FY26. Although the contribution from Unit II has increased, Unit I remains the largest revenue-generating facility. Any breakdown, shutdown, or production disruption at Unit I could affect order execution, sales, and profitability.

The company's inventories increased from Rs 20.57 crore in FY24 to Rs 24.61 crore in FY25 and Rs 51.15 crore in FY26. Trade receivables also increased from Rs 11.61 crore to Rs 21.32 crore and Rs 37.36 crore, respectively, while receivables as a percentage of revenue rose from 13.14% to 15.25% and 17.75%. Failure to manage inventory or collect customer payments on time could increase working capital requirements, borrowing costs, and liquidity pressure.

ipos.name: HGS India
ipos.about:
HGS (India) Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of geophones, geophone strings, seismic cables, geophysical connectors, and related parts and accessories for the seismic industry. Established in 1986, the company manufactures equipment used to record and transmit ground vibrations for analysing underground geological structures.
Its product portfolio includes geophone elements, geophone strings, seismographs, accelerographs, seismometers, seismic system cables, connectors, battery chargers, weight drops, and pig tracking systems. These products are used in oil and gas exploration, mineral exploration, defence research, vibration monitoring, seabed surveys, earthquake studies, and academic research. The company also manufactures cables and connectors for resistivity meters and radar equipment.
The company's manufacturing facility is located in Manesar, Haryana. It operates in-house cable extrusion, injection molding, component assembly, and testing facilities. Its products are sold under the "HG" brand. The company also has a wholly owned subsidiary, HGS Products B.V., in the Netherlands, which provides global sales support.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO consists of both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS).​ Proceeds from the OFS will go to the respective selling shareholders, whereas the net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​
Funding the capital expenditure towards replacement of plant and machinery for the existing
manufacturing facility at Manesar, Gurugram — Rs 15.04  crore
Funding the capital expenditure towards backward integration for setting up in-house gold
plating facility — Rs 1.05 crore
Funding the capex for infrastructure development at its existing manufacturing facility at Manesar, Gurugram — Rs 3.26 crore
Pursuing unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes
strengths: HGS (India) Limited has been operating in the seismic equipment manufacturing industry since 1986. Its products cater to several industries, including oil and gas exploration, mineral exploration, earthquake seismology, defence research, and vibration monitoring.

The company has an international presence, with its products sold in around 47 countries, including India, as of April 30, 2026. Its export revenue increased from Rs 22.41 crore (63.17% of revenue from operations) in FY24 to Rs 29.03 crore (59.15%) in FY25 and Rs 38.04 crore (84.22%) in FY26.

The company claims to have in-house manufacturing capabilities, including precision geophone assembly, cable extrusion, injection moulding, coil winding, magnetising, and product testing. Its Manesar facility is equipped with machinery such as extruders, stranders, braiders, winders, and injection molding machines.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for quality management systems and has received ZED Gold Certification (Zero Defect Zero Effect) from the Ministry of MSME. It also claims to conduct specialised tests, including resistance, frequency, sensitivity, distortion, water leakage, and shaker testing.

The company has established relationships with domestic and international customers. In FY26, it served 149 customers, including domestic and overseas buyers, of which around 51 had placed repeat orders during the preceding three financial years.

The company has developed specialised seismic sensors, including the HG-5VHS high-sensitivity sensor and HG-2 low-frequency sensor, which have entered the initial stage of commercialisation. It has also developed a geophone sensor network for avalanche detection and monitoring, which it states has been deployed with specialised government institutions.

The company has reported a consistent increase in profit after tax (PAT) over the last three financial years. Its PAT increased from Rs 4.00 crore in FY24 to Rs 10.50 crore in FY25 and Rs 11.64 crore in FY26.
risks: The company depends on a limited number of customers for a significant portion of its revenue. Revenue from its top 10 customers amounted to Rs 21.73 crore (61.24%) in FY24, Rs 27.60 crore (56.24%) in FY25 and Rs 32.78 crore (72.58%) in FY26. The company has no long-term contracts with most customers, and the loss of major customers could affect revenue and profitability.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from exports. Export revenue amounted to Rs 22.41 crore (63.17%) in FY24, Rs 29.03 crore (59.15%) in FY25 and Rs 38.04 crore (84.22%) in FY26. Changes in international trade policies, tariffs, geopolitical conditions, or demand in key overseas markets could adversely affect the company's business and financial performance.

The company depends heavily on geophone strings/harnesses and seismic cables for its revenue. Revenue from geophone strings/harnesses accounted for 66.98% in FY24, 51.15% in FY25, and 66.29% in FY26, while seismic cables contributed 23.06%, 26.95%, and 20.39%, respectively. Any decline in demand or inability to upgrade these products could affect its financial performance.

The company has reported low capacity utilisation across several product categories. Capacity utilisation for geophone strings/harnesses declined from 27.07% in FY25 to 13.63% in FY26, while that of seismic cables (units) declined from 64.99% to 24.32%. Continued underutilisation, or an inability to utilise expanded capacity, could affect operating efficiency and profitability.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from oil and gas exploration and geophysical seabed surveys. Revenue from oil and gas exploration amounted to Rs 10.71 crore (30.20%) in FY24, Rs 16.61 crore (33.84%) in FY25 and Rs 12.51 crore (27.70%) in FY26. Meanwhile, revenue from geophysical seabed surveys stood at Rs 6.16 crore (17.37%), Rs 14.05 crore (28.62%) and Rs 12.64 crore (27.99%), respectively. Any slowdown in these industries could adversely affect demand for the company's products.

The company maintains substantial inventories and trade receivables. Inventories stood at Rs 42.38 crore in FY24, Rs 37.96 crore in FY25, and Rs 45.32 crore in FY26, while trade receivables increased from Rs 1.44 crore to Rs 2.80 crore and Rs 3.85 crore, respectively, during this period. Failure to manage inventories or collect outstanding payments could affect its liquidity and working capital requirements.

The company depends on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials and components. Purchases from its top 10 suppliers amounted to Rs 5.50 crore (81.39%) in FY24, Rs 8.82 crore (77.12%) in FY25 and Rs 11.60 crore (69.32%) in FY26. The company has no long-term supply agreements with these suppliers, and any procurement disruption could affect production and profitability.

The company relies heavily on imported raw materials and components. Imports amounted to Rs 4.03 crore (59.58% of total purchases) in FY24, Rs 7.89 crore (68.99%) in FY25 and Rs 12.32 crore (73.65%) in FY26. Adverse changes in foreign exchange rates, import restrictions, or international supply chains could increase procurement costs and affect profitability.
The company and its promoters and directors are involved in certain ongoing legal proceedings. Any adverse judgments in these cases could affect the company's financial condition and operations.

The company's wholly owned subsidiary, HGS Products B.V., Netherlands, incurred a loss of Rs 0.08 crore in FY24. Future operating losses or the need for additional financial support could weigh on the company’s operations and financials.

ipos.name: Bombay Coated & Special Steels
ipos.about:
Bombay Coated and Special Steels Limited is a steel processing company that converts steel coils into processed steel products for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and original design manufacturers (ODMs). Its products include slit coils, embossed slit coils, blanks, embossed blanks, and sheared blanks. The company processes coated, hot-rolled, non-coated, and galvanised steel coils for applications in home appliances, automotive manufacturing, electrical equipment, refrigeration, ventilation systems, and pharmaceutical cleanroom infrastructure. It also provides logistics and inventory management services to support the supply of processed steel products to customers.
The company operates four manufacturing facilities located in Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra, Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh. These facilities are equipped with slitting, cut-to-length, shearing, and embossing lines. As of June 30, 2026, the company had an aggregate installed processing capacity of 123,153 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA). Since 2021, it has been an authorised service partner of JSW Steel Coated Products Limited.
strengths: The company has been an authorised service partner of JSW Steel Coated Products Limited (JSWSCPL) since 2021. JSWSCPL accounted for 85.13%, 86.65%, 90.61%, and 84.58% of the company’s total steel coil purchases in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and original design manufacturers (ODMs), including Haier Appliances India, IFB Refrigeration, Amber Enterprises India, Dixon Electro Manufacturing and Western Refrigeration. Revenue from existing customers accounted for 98.05%, 96.08%, 93.76% and 87.88% of revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and FY26, FY25 and FY24, respectively.

The company operates manufacturing facilities in Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra, Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh. Their locations near industrial clusters and customer manufacturing units support regional supply and reduce transportation time and costs.

The company claims to have processing infrastructure comprising slitting, cut-to-length, shearing, and embossing lines. As of June 30, 2026, its installed capacities included 123,153 MTPA for slitting, 50,481 MTPA for cut-to-length processing, 1,467 MTPA for shearing, and 11,700 MTPA for embossing.

The company’s manufacturing facilities are ISO 9001:2015 certified for quality management systems. The company also states that it follows quality control procedures established jointly with JSWSCPL to maintain product specifications and consistency.
As of June 30, 2026, the company served 178 customers across home and commercial appliances, automotive, electrical equipment, refrigeration, ventilation and other industrial sectors.

The company has shown a consistent increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT) in FY24, FY25, and FY26. Revenue from operations increased from Rs 752.26 crore in FY24 to Rs 1,055.71 crore in FY25 to Rs 1,266.82 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 21.14 crore to Rs 28.67 crore and Rs 30.54 crore over the same period.
risks: The company depends substantially on JSW Steel Coated Products Ltd (JSWSCPL) for its steel coil requirements. JSWSCPL accounted for Rs 239.77 crore (85.13%) of total steel coil purchases in the three months ended June 30, 2026; Rs 1,034.21 crore (86.65%) in FY26; Rs 869.18 crore (90.61%) in FY25; and Rs 557.94 crore (84.58%) in FY24. Any disruption in supplies, adverse changes in commercial terms, or termination of the authorised service partner arrangement could affect the company’s production, customer deliveries, and profitability.

The company reported negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 0.68 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 35.03 crore in FY26, Rs 41.76 crore in FY25, and Rs 52.85 crore in FY24. These outflows were primarily due to purchases of capital assets and increases in other non-current financial assets and other non-current assets, partly offset by changes in fixed or restricted bank deposits, proceeds from the sale of capital assets, and interest income. The company also reported negative cash flows from financing activities of Rs 73.34 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with positive cash flows of Rs 33.71 crore in FY26, Rs 11.57 crore in FY25 and Rs 39.56 crore in FY24. Any continued negative cash flows could affect the company’s ability to meet working capital requirements, service its debt, fund capital expenditure and implement expansion plans without raising additional funds, which may adversely affect its business and financial condition.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from its top 10 customers, which contributed Rs 292.01 crore (73.54%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 903.60 crore (71.33%) in FY26, Rs 712.01 crore (67.44%) in FY25, and Rs 509.28 crore (67.43%) in FY24. Any loss of key customers or reduction in orders due to commercial disputes, financial difficulties, lower demand or operational disruptions could adversely affect the company’s revenue, financial condition and cash flows.

The cost of raw materials and components consumed accounted for Rs 330.17 crore (87.60% of total expenses) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 1,112.37 crore (90.51%) in FY26, Rs 949.71 crore (92.97%) in FY25 and Rs 657.11 crore (89.14%) in FY24. The company is exposed to fluctuations in steel coil prices and supply disruptions, which could increase production costs, affect profit margins, and delay customer deliveries. Any inability to pass on higher costs to customers or procure sufficient steel coils at commercially acceptable prices could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company had a debt-to-equity ratio of 2 times as of June 30, 2026, compared with 2.78 times in FY26, 3.33 times in FY25, and 4.31 times in FY24. Its debt obligations expose it to interest costs, reduced financial flexibility, and risks arising from changes in interest rates or non-compliance with loan covenants. Inability to service debt obligations or refinance borrowings on favourable terms could adversely affect the company’s liquidity, financial condition and ability to fund its growth plans.

The company, its promoters, directors, and certain members of the promoter group are involved in outstanding legal and regulatory proceedings. Any adverse outcome in these proceedings could hurt the company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows. However, no criminal or regulatory proceedings are pending against its key managerial personnel or senior management as of the date of the red herring prospectus.

The company had consolidated outstanding borrowings of Rs 302.43 crore as of August 31, 2026. The company’s indebtedness and related financing obligations could increase its financial costs and affect its cash flows and financial condition.

As of June 30, 2026, Bombay Coated and Special Steels Limited had trade receivables amounting to Rs 165.41 crore. Any failure to collect these receivables on time or at all could adversely affect the company’s cash flows and financial condition.

ipos.name: Carver Roboweld
ipos.about:
̌Carver Roboweld Limited is a manufacturer of welding consumables and provides engineering services to the forging industry. Its products include metal-cored wires, welding rods, gauging electrodes, welding spare parts, and accessories used in welding operations and equipment maintenance. The company also offers forging die regeneration and welding robot rental services.
Its subsidiary, Carver Engineering Private Limited, provides reconditioning and refurbishment services for plant and machinery across industries such as forging, casting, cement, steel, sugar, power, petroleum, automotive, and fabrication. Its services include hammer and component repairs, structural fabrication, machining, and turnkey engineering projects.
The company’s primary manufacturing facility is located in Rajkot, Gujarat. It also operates service units in Pune, Hosur, and Ludhiana. As of July 11, 2026, its installed annual production capacity for metal-cored wires and welding rods was 650 tonnes. The company sources raw materials from domestic suppliers and international markets, including China, the United States, and the Netherlands.
strengths: The company’s promoters, Ranjit Chandrabhai Bose, Rajit Chandra Bose, and Deval Ranjitbhai Bose, collectively have around 16 years of experience in the welding industry. Their experience covers welding consumables manufacturing, robotic welding, process improvement, and business development.

The company operates a manufacturing facility in Bamanbore, Rajkot, Gujarat, and service units in Pune, Ludhiana, and Hosur. This network enables it to serve customers across western, southern, and northern India.

The company serves customers across several states, including Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Gujarat, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Telangana. Its geographical reach spans multiple regions of India, allowing it to cater to customers across different industrial markets.

The company owns 12 welding robots and provides them to customers on a rental basis. Under this arrangement, customers must use the company’s welding consumables, including metal-cored wires, creating demand for these products alongside rental income over the lease tenure.

The company manufactures metal-cored wires, welding rods, and gauging electrodes and supplies welding spare parts and accessories. It also provides forging die regeneration and welding robot rental services, while its subsidiary, Carver Engineering Private Limited, offers machinery reconditioning, repairs, fabrication, machining, and turnkey engineering projects.

The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for the sales of welding consumables, including welding electrodes and metal-cored wires, and for the manufacturing and supply of welding electrodes. It is also a Sustaining Corporate Member of the American Welding Society (AWS).
risks: The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from a limited number of customers. Its top 10 customers contributed Rs 6.68 crore (86.73%) in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs 21.83 crore (80.78%) in FY26, Rs 21.07 crore (84.77%) in FY25, and Rs 15.89 crore (73.34%) in FY24. Any loss of these customers or reduction in business from them could adversely affect the company’s revenue, profitability, and cash flows.

The company’s purchases are heavily dependent on a limited number of suppliers. Its top 10 suppliers accounted for Rs 3.07 crore (90.82%) of total purchases in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs 14.03 crore (92.43%) in FY26, Rs 11.98 crore (94.26%) in FY25, and Rs 9.34 crore (87.15%) in FY24. Any disruption in relationships with these suppliers, or an inability to find suitable alternatives on acceptable terms, could adversely affect the company’s operations and profitability.

The company derives its entire revenue from customers operating in the forging industry. Revenue from these customers amounted to Rs 7.71 crore (100%) in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs 27.02 crore (100%) in FY26, Rs 24.86 crore (100%) in FY25, and Rs 21.67 crore (100%) in FY24. Any slowdown in the forging industry or decline in demand from end-user sectors such as automotive, infrastructure, and engineering could adversely affect the company’s revenue and profitability.

A substantial portion of the company’s revenue comes from Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu. These states contributed Rs 6.56 crore (85.08%) in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs 22.26 crore (82.33%) in FY26, Rs 21.43 crore (86.20%) in FY25, and Rs 17.41 crore (80.33%) in FY24. Any adverse economic, political, regulatory, or social developments in these states could negatively affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company has reported negative cash flows from operating, investing, and financing activities in certain periods. In FY26, net cash used in operating activities was negative Rs 2.65 crore, primarily due to increases in inventories, short-term loans and advances, and trade receivables, along with a decrease in trade payables. Net cash used in investing activities was Rs 1.15 crore in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, mainly due to the purchase of fixed assets, and Rs 6.04 crore in FY26, primarily due to the purchase of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and investments. Net cash used in financing activities was Rs 3.80 crore in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, mainly due to repayments of short-term and long-term borrowings and interest payments, and Rs 0.62 crore in FY26, primarily due to repayments of borrowings and interest, partly offset by proceeds from share capital and long-term borrowings. Continued negative cash flows, higher working capital requirements, capital expenditure, or repayment obligations could adversely affect the company’s liquidity and its ability to meet financial commitments and fund future growth.

The company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 13.43 crore as of October 10, 2026. Any failure to service or repay its borrowings on time could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company had trade receivables of Rs 6.16 crore on a standalone basis as of June 30, 2026. Delays in collecting outstanding amounts from customers could increase its working capital requirements and affect its cash flows. Any failure to recover these receivables on time or in full could adversely affect the company’s liquidity and financial condition.

ipos.name: M. K. Sons Fine Jewels
ipos.about:
M. K. Sons Fine Jewels Limited is a retail jewellery company that sells gold, diamond, and cubic zirconia (CZ) jewellery through its chain of showrooms.
The company's product portfolio includes rings, earrings, necklaces, chains, bangles, bracelets, pendants, mangalsutras, and other jewellery items for everyday wear, weddings, and other occasions. As of June 30, 2026, the company had 19,442 stock-keeping units (SKUs), comprising over 14,582 gold jewellery designs and 4,860 designs featuring diamonds and other precious stones. It also offers customised jewellery designs, gemstone selections, and personalised engravings.
The company operates five company-owned, company-operated (COCO) retail showrooms, of which three are in Mumbai and two in Ahmedabad, with a total operational area of 6,513 square feet. It primarily procures finished jewellery from third-party manufacturers and wholesalers in Maharashtra and Gujarat, while also working with Karigars and an in-house design team for select jewellery designs.
strengths: The company offers jewellery across 11 distinct collections, covering gold, diamond and cubic zirconia (CZ) jewellery. Its collections include traditional bridal jewellery, everyday wear, men's jewellery, religious jewellery and customised designs, with approximate prices ranging from Rs 11,000 to Rs 85 lakh.

The company has recorded consistent growth in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 217.32 crore in FY24 to Rs 351.28 crore in FY25 and Rs 538.74 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 8.17 crore to Rs 23.26 crore and Rs 51.80 crore, respectively.

The company has expanded its customer base, with the number of unique customers increasing from 12,042 in FY24 to 18,000 in FY25 and 24,274 in FY26. The number of new customers also increased from 11,787 to 15,821 and 21,952, respectively.

The company has established a presence across digital platforms, with over 5.91 lakh followers on Instagram, 76,800 subscribers on YouTube and 43,000 followers on Pinterest as of the RHP date. It also participated in 16 exhibitions during FY26 and undertakes advertising campaigns targeting customers across more than 18 Indian states.

The company claims to have an internal inventory management system that enables real-time stock monitoring, barcode tracking, inter-branch transfers, and stock reconciliation across its showrooms. It also uses Tally ERP to record purchases, sales, stock movements, and inventory valuations.

The company deals in gold jewellery certified under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) hallmarking requirements. It also states that its diamond jewellery is accompanied by certifications from gemological laboratories such as the International Gemological Institute (IGI) and/or the Gemological Institute of America (GIA).
risks: The company's revenue from its Gujarat showrooms stood at Rs 162.54 crore, Rs 271.10 crore, and Rs 366.16 crore, accounting for 74.79%, 77.17%, and 67.97% of total revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Its C.G. Road showroom in Ahmedabad alone generated Rs 307.95 crore in FY26, accounting for 57.16% of total revenue. Any adverse developments affecting Gujarat or the C.G. Road showroom could significantly impact the company's revenue, profitability, and overall financial performance.

The company generated its entire revenue from operations of Rs 217.32 crore, Rs 351.28 crore, and Rs 538.74 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively, through five physical showrooms. With no revenue from online sales or alternative distribution channels, any decline in customer footfall or disruption to showroom operations could directly affect its financial performance.

The company relies entirely on third-party manufacturers and Karigars for jewellery production, without long-term contractual arrangements or exclusive manufacturing relationships. Any supply disruption, production delays, or unauthorised disclosure of jewellery designs could adversely affect its operations, profitability, and financial performance.

The company recorded negative cash flows from operating activities amounting to Rs 23.55 crore and Rs 9.53 crore in FY24 and FY25, respectively, primarily due to increased inventory and working capital requirements. It also recorded negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 0.87 crore, Rs 2.34 crore, and Rs 2.93 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively, primarily due to capital expenditure on the purchase of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets; and negative cash flows from financing activities of Rs 9.77 crore in FY26, primarily due to lease principal repayments and finance costs. Sustained cash outflows exceeding inflows could adversely affect the company's liquidity and financial position.

The company's working capital gap increased from Rs 60.49 crore in FY24 to Rs 183.15 crore in FY25 and Rs 240.49 crore in FY26. As of June 30, 2026, its outstanding borrowings stood at Rs 70.52 crore, while its working capital gap reached Rs 266.38 crore. Any inability to secure additional financing on favourable terms could affect its operations and expansion plans.

The company had a portfolio of over 19,442 jewellery SKUs as of June 30, 2026, but its designs were not registered under the Designs Act, 2000. This could limit its ability to prevent competitors from replicating its designs or pursuing legal remedies against unauthorised copying.

The company's inventories increased from Rs 87.48 crore in FY24 to Rs 205.70 crore in FY25 and Rs 256.43 crore in FY26, reaching Rs 275.23 crore as of June 30, 2026. Its inventory holding period increased from 122 days in FY24 to 178 days in FY25 and 193 days in FY26, reaching 333 days for the three months ended June 30, 2026, on a non-annualised basis. High inventory levels and long inventory holding periods could increase working capital requirements and financing costs.

The company's revenue during the third and fourth quarters collectively stood at Rs 173.95 crore, Rs 205.86 crore, and Rs 357.07 crore, accounting for 80.04%, 58.61%, and 66.28% of annual revenue in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. A decline in jewellery demand during weddings and festive seasons could disproportionately affect its annual financial performance.

Revenue from gold jewellery stood at Rs 194.35 crore, Rs 298.39 crore, and Rs 471.08 crore, contributing 89.43%, 84.94%, and 87.44% of revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Since gold jewellery generally carries lower margins than diamond-studded and designer jewellery, continued dependence on gold sales could constrain the company's profitability.

ipos.name: Ajwa Projects
ipos.about:
Ajwa Projects Limited provides industrial engineering, fabrication, erection, piping, maintenance, and civil construction services. The company undertakes structural fabrication work involving industrial buildings, girders, platforms, heavy modules, and other steel structures. It also manufactures equipment such as pressure vessels, boilers, heat exchangers, tanks, chimneys, ducts, and specialised industrial components.
The company's services include installing and assembling industrial structures, equipment, and piping systems. It also undertakes civil construction activities, including site preparation, earthworks, foundations, factory buildings, and supporting infrastructure. The company also provides prefabricated structures, mechanical maintenance, non-destructive testing, sandblasting, and industrial painting services.
Ajwa Projects serves industries including oil and gas, refineries, power generation, steel, cement, chemicals, and transportation infrastructure. The company operates a workshop facility at Ichchapore GIDC in Surat, Gujarat, and carries out fabrication and installation activities at client project sites.
strengths: As of October 5, 2026, Ajwa Projects Limited was executing more than 26 projects, with an outstanding order book valued at Rs 42.43 crore.

The company has witnessed consistent growth in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 34.26 crore in FY24 to Rs 36.73 crore in FY25 and Rs 48.42 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 2.95 crore to Rs 3.28 crore and Rs 5.42 crore, respectively.

The company claims to have a flexible execution model that allows it to undertake fabrication activities at its workshops as well as directly at client project sites. Its operations cover structural fabrication, piping, pressure equipment, erection, and civil construction works.
The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified for quality management systems and ISO 45001:2018 certified for occupational health and safety management systems.
The company has undertaken projects across industries such as oil and gas, refineries, petrochemicals, steel, power, cement, fertilisers, bridges, metro rail, and bullet train infrastructure.
The company claims to have a workforce of 557 personnel, including skilled, semi-skilled, and supervisory staff, deployed across its fabrication facilities and client project sites.
risks: The company, its promoters, and directors are involved in certain ongoing legal proceedings. Any adverse judgments in any of these cases could be detrimental to the company’s business prospects.

The company's top 10 customers contributed Rs 12.22 crore (98.52%), Rs 41.96 crore (86.65%), Rs 28.66 crore (78.03%), and Rs 29.67 crore (86.58%) to its revenue from operations for the period ended June 30, 2026, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any failure to retain these customers or a reduction in business from them could adversely affect the company's revenue and financial performance.

The company's revenue is geographically concentrated in Gujarat, which contributed Rs 11.94 crore (96.24%), Rs 45.50 crore (93.96%), Rs 29.48 crore (80.26%), and Rs 23.27 crore (67.91%) to its revenue from operations for the period ended June 30, 2026, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any adverse developments in Gujarat could significantly affect the company's operations and financial performance.

The company recorded negative cash flows from operating activities amounting to Rs 0.98 crore, Rs 2.88 crore, and Rs 1.17 crore for the period ended June 30, 2026, FY26, and FY24, respectively, primarily due to increased inventories and trade receivables. It also recorded negative cash flows from investing activities amounting to Rs 0.15 crore, Rs 0.36 crore, Rs 0.12 crore, and Rs 1.22 crore for the period ended June 30, 2026, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Additionally, it recorded negative cash flow from financing activities amounting to Rs 4.50 crore in FY25. If cash outflows continue to exceed inflows, the company may face liquidity challenges in the future.

As of June 30, 2026, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 13.84 crore, comprising secured and unsecured borrowings. Any failure to service these borrowings or comply with the restrictive covenants under its financing agreements could adversely affect its operations and financial position.

The company's top 10 suppliers accounted for Rs 3.33 crore (66.24%), Rs 2.94 crore (80.21%), Rs 12.92 crore (58.66%), and Rs 5.15 crore (67.16%) of its total cost of materials consumed in FY24, FY25, FY26, and six months ending September 2026, respectively. The company also depends on client-nominated vendors for several raw materials. Any disruption in supplies could delay project execution and increase procurement costs.

The company has experienced delays and discrepancies in statutory filings with the Registrar of Companies, including 26 instances of delayed filings. Some delays extended to 474 days, and any recurrence of such non-compliance could result in penalties or regulatory action.

The company has experienced delays in filing returns and depositing statutory dues relating to GST, TDS, provident fund, professional tax, and ESIC. Although the company states that no related dues remain outstanding as of the prospectus date, any future non-compliance could result in penalties and additional financial liabilities.

ipos.name: BLS Polymers
ipos.about:
BLS Polymers is a manufacturer of custom-formulated polymer compounds used in the wire and cable, infrastructure, and other industries. Its products are used for insulation, sheathing, jacketing, and protective coating of wires, cables, and underground pipelines. The company’s product portfolio includes high-density polyethylene (HDPE), medium-density polyethylene (MDPE), linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE), cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE), halogen-free flame-retardant (HFFR), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), cable filling compounds (CFC), and adhesive coating compounds. 
These products are used in applications across the power, telecommunications, railways, water, and oil and gas distribution industries. HDPE, MDPE, and LLDPE compounds are used in wire and cable insulation and protection, while XLPE, HFFR, PVC, and CFC compounds serve applications requiring properties such as electrical insulation, fire resistance, and moisture resistance. HDPE and adhesive coating compounds are also used in three-layer polyethylene (3LPE) coatings for oil, gas, and water pipelines.
strengths: BLS Polymers has enlisted several products with government agencies and public sector enterprises, including a Maharatna CPSE power transmission company, a Navratna CPSE engineering consultancy company, a Miniratna CPSE telecommunications company, and the Government of Gujarat. These approvals cover products used in wire and cable manufacturing, oil and gas pipelines, and water pipelines.

As of August 31, 2026, the company manufactured six product categories across 127 grades, including PE, XLPE, PVC, CFC, HFFR, and pipe coating compounds. These products cater to applications in power cables, telecommunications, railway signalling, and oil, gas, and water distribution pipelines.

As of August 31, 2026, BLS Polymers has an in-house product development team of seven employees. The team has developed pipe coating adhesives for underground oil, gas, and water pipelines, and the products have received certification from Bureau Veritas for compliance with standards including ISO 21809-1:2018 and DIN 30670:2012.

The company sold its products in 23 states and Union Territories during the three months ended June 30, 2026, and the preceding three financial years. Its domestic operations accounted for 94.68% of revenue from operations during the three months ended June 30, 2026.

The company has shown a consistent increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT) in FY24, FY25, and FY26. Revenue from operations increased from Rs 296.36 crore in FY24 to Rs 328.43 crore in FY25 to Rs 349.43 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 7.52 crore to Rs 21.14 crore and Rs 27.01 crore over the same period.
risks: The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from the sale of wire and cable polymer compounds, which contributed Rs 78.34 crore (73.20%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 282.80 crore (80.93%) in FY26, Rs 267.98 crore (81.59%) in FY25, and Rs 238.53 crore (80.49%) in FY24. A reduction in demand for these products, a downturn in the wire and cable industry, or an inability to diversify its product portfolio and retain customers could adversely affect the company’s revenue, profitability, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from its top 10 customers, who contributed Rs 65.65 crore (61.34%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 233.47 crore (66.81%) in FY26, Rs 211.67 crore (64.44%) in FY25, and Rs 149.74 crore (50.52%) in FY24. Any loss of these customers, reduction or cancellation of orders, or inability to maintain existing order volumes and pricing terms could adversely affect the company’s revenue, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.

The company reported negative cash flows from operating activities of Rs 4.08 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and negative cash flows from investing activities of Rs 5.79 crore during the same period. Negative investing cash flows were also reported in FY26, FY24, and the three months ended June 30, 2026, primarily due to additions to property, plant and equipment, including plant and machinery to increase production capacity. The company also reported negative cash flows from financing activities of Rs 31.05 crore in FY26, Rs 25.72 crore in FY25, and Rs 2.24 crore in FY24, mainly due to repayments of unsecured loans from a group company and working capital demand loans, as well as higher interest payments on bank borrowings in FY24. Sustained or significant negative cash flows in the future could adversely affect the company’s financial condition, operations, and growth plans.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from repeat orders, which contributed Rs 97.23 crore (90.84%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 337.24 crore (96.51%) in FY26, Rs 305.57 crore (93.04%) in FY25, and Rs 241.98 crore (81.65%) in FY24. Its ability to retain repeat orders depends on maintaining product quality, competitive pricing, and timely deliveries. Failure to meet customer requirements, urgent demand, or quality expectations, disputes, termination of existing arrangements, or deterioration in customers’ financial conditions could reduce repeat orders and adversely affect the company’s revenue, profitability, financial condition, and cash flows. Acquiring new customers also involves additional marketing and onboarding expenses.

The company depends on a limited number of suppliers for key raw materials, including LLDPE resin, HDPE resin, and recycled HDPE, which accounted for 76.62% of revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026, 78.13% in FY26, 80.85% in FY25, and 83.90% in FY24. Its top 10 suppliers accounted for 88.02% of total procurement costs during the three months ended June 30, 2026, 93.52% in FY26, 83.52% in FY25, and 75.34% in FY24. The company has not entered into long-term supply agreements with most suppliers, leaving it exposed to supply interruptions, delays, shortages, quality issues, and suppliers serving competitors. Raw material price increases due to market pressures, supply chain disruptions, or government restrictions may also reduce profit margins if the company cannot pass higher costs on to customers. Advance payments to international suppliers further expose the company to the risk of non-delivery or inadequate supplies.

The company operates a single manufacturing facility in Goa, spread across approx. 24,220 sq. m. A disruption or shutdown at this facility due to natural disasters, social unrest, regulatory action, equipment breakdowns, industrial accidents, labour disputes, power or water shortages, or interruptions in raw material supplies could affect production and delay customer orders. The facility was temporarily shut down for about 21 days during the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020. Although no other material operational disruptions were reported during the three months ended June 30, 2026, or FY26, FY25, and FY24, any future shutdown could reduce sales, increase costs associated with alternative production arrangements, and adversely affect the company’s business, cash flows, results of operations, and financial condition.

The company had contingent liabilities of Rs 10.94 crore as of June 30, 2026. If a significant portion of these liabilities materialise, or if adverse developments in ongoing matters require additional provisions, the company’s expenses, liabilities, cash flows, and financial condition could be adversely affected.

The company had trade receivables of Rs 95.15 crore as of June 30, 2026, indicating a significant amount of funds outstanding from its customers. Any delay or failure in recovering these receivables could adversely affect the company’s cash flows, working capital position, and financial condition.

The company had consolidated outstanding borrowings of Rs 82.35 crore as of August 31, 2026. The company’s indebtedness and related financing obligations could increase its financial costs and affect its cash flows and financial condition.

ipos.name: SFC Environmental Technologies
ipos.about:
SFC Environmental Technologies Ltd is an environmental technology company incorporated in 2005. The company provides technologies and engineering solutions for wastewater treatment, wastewater recycling and reuse, and solid waste treatment.
Its wastewater treatment operations include designing, manufacturing, supplying, supervising installation, and commissioning treatment equipment. It uses its proprietary C-Tech technology to treat sewage and effluents. The company also offers turbo blowers, fibre disc filters, solar sludge drying systems, and membrane-based treatment technologies. Its wastewater recycling and reuse solutions include ultrafiltration, closed-circuit reverse osmosis, and membrane bioreactor technologies.
In solid waste treatment, the company provides plant design, engineering, construction, installation, commissioning, and operations and maintenance services. Its proprietary OREX technology separates biodegradable organic matter from inorganic materials in municipal solid waste. The company operates two integrated solid waste treatment facilities in Goa, with a combined treatment capacity of 350 tonnes per day and an additional handling capacity of 75 tonnes per day. Through its subsidiaries, it is also involved in compressed biogas projects using municipal and agricultural waste.
strengths: According to the prospectus, SFC Environment was the first technology provider to introduce sequencing batch reactor (SBR) technology through its C-Tech system in India. As of July 31, 2026, the company had commissioned 728 wastewater treatment installations and claims to hold over 80% market share in SBR technology in India.

The company claims to have developed in-house manufacturing capabilities for components used in its C-Tech and OREX technologies, including decanters, diffusers, turbo blowers, and solar sludge drying systems. It has also entered into technology and supply agreements with international companies, including TurboMax Company Limited of South Korea, IST-Anlagenbau GmbH of Germany, and EDI Inc. of the USA.

The company operates two integrated solid waste treatment facilities in Goa for the Goa Waste Management Corporation, with a combined treatment capacity of 350 tonnes per day and an additional handling capacity of 75 tonnes per day. According to the prospectus, its Saligao plant in North Goa has operated for over 10 years and recorded an average biogas yield of more than 150 Nm³ per tonne of organic waste in the last financial year.

Through its wholly owned subsidiary, HWTPL, the company has secured orders from a public sector oil marketing company for two compressed biogas plants. These include a 125-tonne-per-day plant in Tinsukia, Assam, and a 300-tonne-per-day plant in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, with a combined order value of Rs 501.70 crore. The contracts include engineering, procurement, commissioning, and operations and maintenance for 10 years.
As of August 31, 2026, the company’s total order book stood at Rs 1,656.64 crore across wastewater treatment, wastewater recycling and reuse, and solid waste treatment.

The company has shown a consistent increase in revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT) in FY24, FY25, and FY26. Revenue from operations increased from Rs 657.49 crore in FY24 to Rs 697.86 crore in FY25 to Rs 803.63 crore in FY26, while PAT increased from Rs 144.17 crore to Rs 152.01 crore and Rs 160.21 crore over the same period.
risks: SFC Environment derives 88.22%, 84.98%, 84.34%, and 87.40% of its consolidated revenue from operations from its wastewater treatment (WWT) and solid waste treatment (SWT) segments in the three months ended June 30, 2026, FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Revenue attributable to government entities or government tenders accounted for 91.97%, 92.35%, 92.40%, and 95.72% of the WWT segment’s revenue during these periods, while the SWT segment derived 100% of its revenue from such sources in each period. Adverse changes in government policies, budgetary allocations, or tender awards, or reductions or terminations of government-funded projects, could hurt the company’s business and financial condition.

The company’s top 10 customers contributed Rs 106.09 crore (79.20%) in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 517.84 crore (64.44%) in FY26, Rs 428.28 crore (61.37%) in FY25, and Rs 389.11 crore (59.18%) in FY24 to its revenue from operations. The company does not generally enter into long-term contracts with customers in its WWT and WRR segments, relying instead on purchase orders or letters of intent that can be terminated with or without notice. Any failure to retain key customers, cancellation or reduction of orders, or delays in payments from major customers could adversely affect the company’s revenue, profitability, and financial condition.

The company reported negative operating cash flows of Rs 21.34 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 25.80 crore in FY26, and Rs 11.69 crore in FY24. These were primarily due to working capital movements, including increases in trade receivables in FY26 and in FY24, along with increases in inventories and other current assets. The company also reported negative investing cash flows of Rs 66.47 crore in FY26 and Rs 77.15 crore in FY24, mainly due to investments in fixed deposits, capital expenditure, acquisitions of subsidiaries, and loans given. Negative financing cash flows of Rs 106.52 crore in FY25 primarily resulted from repayment of borrowings, dividend payments, interest payments, and lease liabilities. Any continued working capital requirements, capital expenditure, acquisitions, or debt repayments could result in further negative cash flows and adversely affect the company’s liquidity and financial condition.

The company’s solid waste treatment (SWT) business requires substantial upfront capital investment and working capital. Project agreements may require equity contributions of up to 25% of project costs and performance bank guarantees of up to 10% of project costs, while investments under concession agreements may be recovered over several years after commissioning. The RBI’s Project Finance Directions, 2025, effective October 1, 2025, require at least 90% of a project’s total financing to be tied up and contractually committed before the first loan disbursement, which could delay financial closure and project commencement. Planned compressed biogas and waste-to-energy projects may also require further equity or capital investments, with funding amounts and timelines yet to be determined. The company may need additional debt or equity financing to meet these requirements, and any difficulty in obtaining funds on favourable terms could increase financing costs, debt obligations, and cash flow pressures, adversely affecting its financial condition and results of operations.

The company is involved in legal proceedings pending before various courts, tribunals, and governmental authorities.
