Any adverse rulings, changes in applicable laws, or developments in these proceedings could require the company to make additional provisions in its financial statements, increase its expenses and current liabilities, and adversely affect its business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.

The company’s top 10 suppliers accounted for Rs 36.99 crore (54.48%) of its purchases of stock-in-trade and raw materials in the three months ended June 30, 2026, Rs 195.26 crore (55.66%) in FY26, Rs 144.28 crore (47.71%) in FY25, and Rs 218.99 crore (63.71%) in FY24. The company generally procures raw materials and components, including decanters, diffusers, spares, and PVC pipes, through purchase orders rather than continuing and exclusive supply agreements. It also relies on imports for key materials, with imported stock-in-trade accounting for 64.24% of purchases in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and 69.12%, 71.67%, and 77.99% in FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any supplier disruption, price increase, delay in imported materials, or difficulty finding alternative suppliers could increase costs, delay project execution, result in contractual claims, and adversely affect the company’s operations, cash flows, and financial condition.

The company has experienced an increase in its cash conversion cycle, which may continue to require significant working capital and adversely affect its liquidity and financial condition. The company’s cash conversion cycle increased from 141 days in FY24 to 259 days in FY25, before declining to 235 days in FY26, and further increased to 569 days in the three months ended June 30, 2026, primarily due to the seasonality of its business and lower revenue during the first half of the financial year. Trade receivable days increased from 197 days in FY24 to 262 days in FY25 and 282 days in FY26, while inventory days increased from 78 days in FY24 to 106 days in FY25 and FY26. A consistent increase in the cash conversion cycle, delays in customer payments, inability to manage inventory efficiently, or a reduction in credit periods extended by suppliers could increase the company’s working capital requirements, result in cash flow mismatches and adversely affect its liquidity, cash flows, financial condition and results of operations.

The company had consolidated outstanding borrowings of Rs 253.10 crore as of July 31, 2026. The company’s indebtedness and related financing obligations could increase its financial costs and affect its cash flows and financial condition.

ipos.name: Wiscon Industries
ipos.about:
Wiscon Industries Limited is a Delhi-based supplier of consumer electronic products in India. Its product portfolio includes LED televisions, air coolers, washing machines, and air conditioners, which are sold under its flagship brand, Wiscon. The company also sells electric scooters under a third-party brand.
The company serves both business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) customers. It conducts its B2B operations through an offline customer network, while it makes B2C sales through its website. Wiscon Industries was incorporated as a public limited company on September 16, 2022. 
In May 2025, the company acquired a 100% stake in Dalmia Technologies Limited (DTL), which manufactures LED televisions and trades in other electronic products. DTL became its wholly owned subsidiary, and the company’s consolidated financial statements include DTL from FY26 onward. Accordingly, consolidated figures for FY26 and the quarter ended June 30, 2026 include DTL’s financial results, while historical figures for FY24 and FY25 in the relevant standalone statements reflect Wiscon Industries on a standalone basis.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO consists of both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS).​ Proceeds from the OFS will go to the respective selling shareholders, whereas the net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​
Investment in the wholly owned subsidiary, Dalmia Technologies Limited for financing its capital expenditure towards purchase of plant and machinery — Rs 15.04 crore
Investment in Dalmia Technologies Limited for funding its incremental working capital requirements — Rs 35 crore
To meet working capital requirements of Wiscon— Rs 17 crore
To fund marketing and promotional activities in the company — Rs 5.22 crore
General corporate purposes
strengths: The company sells LED TVs, air coolers, washing machines, and air conditioners under its Wiscon brand. It also sells electric scooters under a third-party brand, giving it a product portfolio across consumer electronics and electric mobility.

The company sells its products through an offline B2B customer network and its website for B2C sales. In FY26, B2B sales of LED TVs accounted for Rs 49.08 crore (66.87%) of standalone revenue from operations, while electric scooter sales contributed Rs 19.87 crore (27.08%), primarily through B2B customers.
The company’s standalone revenue from operations increased from Rs 3.21 crore in FY24 to Rs 14.49 crore in FY25 and to Rs 73.39 crore in FY26 on a consolidated basis.

The company provides installation, repairs, and customer support through third-party service providers. Services for products covered under warranty are provided free of charge, while repairs outside the warranty period are chargeable.

The company’s promoter and Managing Director, Sidhant Dalmia, has approximately seven years of industry experience. He oversees the company’s business operations, while the sales team manages customer orders and sales activities across India.
risks: The company depends heavily on a small group of suppliers for its product purchases and does not have long-term or exclusive supply agreements with them. On a standalone basis, its top 10 suppliers accounted for Rs 20.82 crore (99.77%) of total purchases in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs 64.35 crore (99.33%) in FY26, Rs 11.71 crore (99.82%) in FY25, and Rs 2.22 crore (99.97%) in FY24. Any disruption in supplies, increase in procurement costs, or inability to find alternative suppliers within the required timelines could adversely affect the company’s operations and profitability.

The company derives a significant portion of its revenue from a limited number of customers and does not have long-term sales contracts with them. On a standalone basis, its top 10 customers contributed Rs 15.41 crore (63.36%) of revenue from operations in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs 49.72 crore (67.75%) in FY26, Rs 9.76 crore (67.34%) in FY25, and Rs 1.53 crore (47.50%) in FY24. Any loss of key customers, reduction in order volumes, or cancellation of purchase orders could adversely affect the company’s revenue, profitability, and financial condition.

The company generates 100% of its revenue from domestic operations, with a significant portion concentrated in Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana. These three regions contributed 74.25% of revenue in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, 83.76% in FY26, Rs 77.42% in FY25, and 55.21% in FY24. Any adverse economic, competitive, or regulatory developments in these regions, or the company’s inability to expand into other markets, could adversely affect its business, revenue, and financial performance.

The company, its directors, promoter, key managerial personnel, senior management personnel, group companies, and wholly owned subsidiary are involved in certain outstanding legal proceedings, including civil and criminal cases, tax matters, and statutory and regulatory actions. Any adverse outcome in these proceedings could result in financial liabilities, penalties, or other restrictions, which may adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and reputation.

The company reported negative net cash flows on a consolidated basis from operating activities of Rs 9.89 crore in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs 20.01 crore in FY26, and on a standalone basis Rs 1.36 crore in FY24, compared with positive operating cash flow on a standalone basis of Rs 0.64 crore in FY25. The negative cash flows in the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and FY26 were primarily due to increases in trade receivables and loans and advances, respectively. The company’s ability to manage working capital and collect outstanding receivables in a timely manner may affect its liquidity and ability to meet its operating and financial obligations.

The company’s trade receivables have increased significantly from Rs 0.21 crore as of FY24, to Rs 3.54 crore as of FY25 on a standalone basis, and then on a consolidated basis it increased to Rs 47.59 crore as of FY26, and Rs 73.62 crore as of June 30, 2026. This sharp increase, alongside negative cash flows from operating activities in FY26 and as of June 30, 2026 indicates that the company has not converted its reported operating performance into cash flows from operations during these periods. Delays or defaults in collecting receivables could further increase working capital requirements, necessitate additional borrowing, and adversely affect the company’s liquidity, cash flows, and financial condition.

The company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 12.10 crore on a standalone basis as of June 30, 2026. Any failure to service or repay its borrowings on time could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

ipos.name: EAAA India Alternatives
ipos.about: EAAA India Alternatives Limited is the alternatives investment arm of Edelweiss Financial Services Limited, positioning itself as one of the leading alternative asset management platforms in India. The company operates two key business verticals: Real Assets, which invests in infrastructure and commercial real estate, and Private Credit, which provides debt financing solutions to corporates and projects. EAAA caters to a diverse client base of global and domestic investors, including institutional investors like pension funds and insurance companies, as well as ultra-high net worth individuals (UHNIs), high net worth individuals (HNIs), and family offices.
strengths: The company operates a diversified, multi-vertical platform across Real Assets and Private Credit, which provides resilience against sector-specific downturns. As of June 30, 2026, the Real Assets and Private Credit verticals contributed 57.67% (FPAUM of ₹2,804 Crores) and 39.64% (FPAUM of ₹1,927.24 Crores) respectively to its total FPAUM.

The company has established a diverse and long-standing client base, with a significant 77% of its AUM as of June 30, 2026, comprising commitments from repeat clients, underscoring strong client trust and retention.

The company operates a dedicated asset management platform through its subsidiary, Sekura, which has a team of 58 operational members and holds multiple ISO certifications, ensuring institutional-grade operational oversight and value enhancement for its portfolio assets.

It has a demonstrated track record of raising capital across market cycles, having raised capital commitments aggregating to ₹4,752.63 Crores in the last three financial years and the first three months of FY27, indicating consistent investor confidence.

The business is led by a seasoned management team with an average experience of approximately 26.12 years, providing stability and deep industry expertise, which is critical for navigating complex alternative investment markets.

The firm's revenue model includes stable and predictable management and advisory fees from close-ended funds, which provide a consistent income base. These fees contributed 60.08%, 60.97%, and 68.12% of total income in FY26, FY25, and FY24 respectively.
risks: A significant and volatile portion of the company's income is derived from Variable Additional Return (VAR), which constituted 30.14% of total income in FY26. The unpredictable timing and realization of this income stream is a key risk, highlighted by the fact that of the ₹684.72 Crores in VAR recognized since FY24, only ₹397.65 Crores has been realized.

The company has experienced periods of negative cash flows from operations, recording a net cash outflow of ₹120.17 Crores in FY25 and ₹13.27 Crores in FY24, primarily due to investments in funds and distributor payouts, which could strain liquidity and affect strategic initiatives if prolonged.

The business is exposed to significant client concentration risk, with the top 10 clients contributing 26.20% of the Fee Paying Assets Under Management (FPAUM) as of June 30, 2026. Any change in investment behavior or withdrawal by these clients could materially impact financial stability.

The company and its promoters are involved in numerous legal and regulatory proceedings, with an aggregate amount of over ₹665.15 Crores, including criminal proceedings of ₹45.08 Crores against the company. An adverse outcome in these material litigations could impact financial position and reputation.

The company has a history of significant dividend payouts, including ₹205.70 Crores in FY26, which may not be sustainable and could be a pre-IPO action to reward existing shareholders. The dividend policy is subject to change and future payouts are not guaranteed.

A significant portion of employee compensation is tied to the realization of Variable Additional Return (VAR), constituting 42.21% of total employee benefit expense in FY26. This structure creates a dual risk: high payouts can reduce profitability, while unfavorable changes could negatively affect employee retention and talent acquisition.

ipos.name: Core4 Engineer
ipos.about:
Core4 Engineers is an engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) company engaged in railway infrastructure, power transmission and distribution, and water and wastewater treatment projects. The company operates across five business segments: railway electrification and infrastructure, extra high-tension transmission and distribution systems, water and wastewater treatment, automation and SCADA systems, and high-tension and low-tension electrical panels and compact substations.
Its railway infrastructure services include overhead electrification, traction substations, signalling interfaces, station redevelopment, and allied civil works. Its power transmission and distribution projects cover substations, transmission lines, and distribution networks up to 220 kV. The company also undertakes turnkey projects for water treatment plants, sewage treatment plants, and effluent treatment plants. Its automation services include PLC-based systems, remote monitoring, and control solutions. The company manufactures HT and LT electrical panels and compact substations with capacities up to 2.5 MVA and voltage levels up to 11 kV at its in-house manufacturing facility.
strengths: Core4 Engineers operates across railway electrification and infrastructure, extra-high-tension transmission and distribution, water and wastewater treatment, SCADA and automation, and electrical panel manufacturing. According to the prospectus, the company has executed projects across several Indian states, with 50 ongoing projects and 24 completed projects across its listed business segments.

As of the filing of the Draft Red Herring Prospectus, the company had an order book of approximately Rs 111.47 crore. The projects span Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Jammu and Kashmir, Odisha, Delhi, Kerala, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Andhra Pradesh.

The company claims to manufacture high-tension (HT) and low-tension (LT) electrical panels at its facility in Karnataka. It manufactures 415-volt and 750-volt LT systems, depending on project requirements, and states that electrical panels account for approximately 20% of the total value of almost all its service projects.

Core4 Engineers claims to have an in-house testing facility certified by the Central Power Research Institute (CPRI), Bengaluru. The company states that it conducts eight prescribed type tests covering temperature rise, mechanical impact protection, ingress protection, dielectric properties and other parameters for its electrical panels and related products.

The company claims to manufacture compact substations with capacities of up to 2.5 MVA and voltage levels of up to 11 kV. These units combine a transformer, HT panel, LT panel, and protection systems in a single enclosure for industrial, commercial, and utility applications.

Core4 Engineers undertakes projects covering design, engineering, procurement, construction, installation, testing and commissioning. Its service portfolio includes 25 kV AC railway overhead electrification, traction substations, transmission projects up to 220 kV, water and wastewater treatment plants, and PLC-based automation systems.

The company has witnessed a consistent increase in its revenue from operations and profit after tax (PAT). Revenue from operations increased from Rs 13.12 crore in FY24 to Rs 33.45 crore in FY25 and Rs 34.16 crore in FY26. PAT increased from Rs 0.84 crore in FY24 to Rs 2.88 crore in FY25 and Rs 3.81 crore in FY26.
risks: Core4 Engineers derives a significant portion of its revenue from government and government-owned customers. Revenue from government and government-owned companies accounted for 27.57% in the six months ended September 30, 2025, 56.43% in FY25, Rs 69.66% in FY24, and 62.90% in FY23. Any adverse changes in government infrastructure spending, budget allocations, project awards, or policies could hurt the company’s revenue, order book, cash flows, and financial performance.

Core4 Engineers derives a significant portion of its revenue from Karnataka, accounting for Rs 41.77 crore (88.75%) in the six months ended September 30, 2025, Rs 14.75 crore (43.17%) in FY25, Rs 13.40 crore (40.06%) in FY24, and Rs 10.13 crore (77.18%) in FY23. All its ongoing projects are located in Karnataka as of the date of the Draft Red Herring Prospectus. Any adverse political, economic, social, or regulatory developments in the state, or a reduction in infrastructure spending, could adversely affect the company’s project execution, revenue, and financial performance.

Core4 Engineers derives a significant portion of its revenue from railway infrastructure projects, accounting for Rs 10.00 crore (21.26%) in the six months ended September 30, 2025, Rs 16.10 crore (47.13%) in FY25, Rs 20.22 crore (60.46%) in FY24, and Rs 4.84 crore (36.91%) in FY23. The company has also faced two contract terminations involving railway infrastructure projects, with related legal proceedings pending. Any reduction in railway sector spending, delays in project approvals or execution, changes in technical requirements, or further contract disputes and terminations could adversely affect the company’s order inflows, revenue, profitability, cash flows, and financial condition.

Core4 Engineers derives a significant portion of its revenue from a limited number of customers. Its top five customers contributed Rs 38.72 crore (82.27%), Rs 17.11 crore (50.09%), Rs 15.46 crore (46.21%), and Rs 6.37 crore (48.60%), respectively, during these periods. The loss of key customers, reduced orders, pricing pressure, payment disputes, or changes in their business requirements could adversely affect the company’s revenue, cash flows, profitability, and financial condition.

Core4 Engineers depends on timely procurement of construction materials and electrical components for its EPC projects and does not have long-term supply agreements with its vendors. Its top 10 suppliers accounted for 47.11%, 41.15%, 44.65%, and 62.71% of purchases, respectively. Any increase in material prices, supply shortages, quality issues, or disruption involving key suppliers could delay project execution, increase procurement costs and working capital requirements, and adversely affect the company’s financial performance and cash flows.

Core4 Engineers faces competition from established EPC companies, regional contractors, public sector undertakings, and new entrants in the public and private sectors. Competitive bidding may put pressure on pricing and margins, while competitors with greater financial resources, technical capabilities, or stronger execution records may be better positioned to secure projects. If the company fails to win new contracts on commercially viable terms, it could see lower order inflows, reduced profitability, underutilisation of resources, and adverse effects on cash flows and its financial condition.

The company had contingent liabilities of Rs 6.27 crore as of September 30, 2026. Any adverse outcome or materialisation of these liabilities could affect the company’s financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

The company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 28.34 crore as of September 30, 2026. Any failure to service or repay its borrowings on time could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and cash flows.

The company had trade receivables of Rs 39.45 crore as of September 30, 2026. Any delay or failure in collecting these receivables could increase working capital requirements and adversely affect the company’s cash flows and financial condition.

ipos.name: Paras Healthcare
ipos.about:
Paras Healthcare is a hospital operator providing tertiary and quaternary healthcare services through a network of eight hospitals under the Paras Health brand. As of June 30, 2026, the company was present in five states and one Union Territory. Its hospitals are located in Gurugram and Panchkula in Haryana, Patna and Darbhanga in Bihar, Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh, Udaipur in Rajasthan, Ranchi in Jharkhand, and Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir.
The company provides treatments across several clinical specialities, including cardiac sciences, oncology sciences, neurosciences, gastro sciences, orthopaedics and sports injury, and renal sciences. As of June 30, 2026, its hospital network had 1,084 doctors and 1,937 nurses. 
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO consists of both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS).​ Proceeds from the OFS will go to the respective selling shareholders, whereas the net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​ 
Prepayment or scheduled repayment, in full or part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by the company — Rs 320.90 crore
Investment in the wholly owned subsidiary, PMHPL, for repayment/prepayment of borrowings, in full or part, of PMHPL — Rs 54.10 crore
General corporate purposes
strengths: As of June 30, 2026, the company operated eight hospitals with an aggregate bed capacity of 2,211 beds across five states and one Union Territory. It claims to have an early-mover advantage in several markets, including being the first corporate hospital entrant among its listed peers in Gurugram and Patna.

The company focuses on cardiac sciences, oncology, neurosciences, gastro sciences, orthopaedics and sports injury, and renal sciences. These specialities contributed 74.70% of its revenue from operations in FY26, compared with 72.34% in FY24.

The company claims to have advanced medical equipment, including surgical robots, LINACs, biplane catheterisation laboratories, PET-CT scanners, and MRI machines. It also offers bone marrow transplant programmes at its Gurugram, Patna, and Panchkula hospitals, along with kidney and liver transplant programmes at Gurugram and Patna.

As of the date of the prospectus, seven of the company’s eight hospitals were accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH). The company also reported a patient satisfaction score of 90.60 and a net promoter score of 93.31 as of March 31, 2026.

The company operates its hospitals through a combination of ownership, fixed-rent arrangements, revenue-sharing agreements, and public-private partnerships. This approach allows it to establish hospitals under different financial and operational arrangements, depending on the market and property requirements.

The company claims to have implemented electronic health records, hospital information systems, business intelligence platforms, and digital patient engagement tools across its hospital network. Its digital systems support functions such as patient registration, appointment booking, clinical documentation, discharge summaries, reporting, and hospital administration.

As of June 30, 2026, the company had 1,084 doctors and 1,937 nurses across its hospital network. It also offers Diplomate of National Board (DNB) and Doctorate of National Board (DrNB) postgraduate programmes across 14 specialities at its Gurugram, Patna, Panchkula, and Udaipur hospitals, with the capacity to train up to 60 students annually.
risks: The company incurred losses of Rs 57.98 crore and Rs 15.33 crore in FY25 and FY24, respectively, and Rs 1.02 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2025. These losses were primarily attributable to the ramp-up of its Srinagar and Kanpur hospitals and investments in bed capacity expansion and clinical programmes across its hospital network. Although the company reported a profit of Rs 43.83 crore in FY26, any failure to increase revenue sufficiently to cover expenses and sustain profitability could adversely affect its financial performance.

The company’s subsidiaries, Paras Healthcare (Ranchi) Private Limited and Plus Medicare Hospitals Private Limited, collectively incurred losses of Rs 20.38 crore, Rs 52.09 crore, Rs 82.24 crore, and Rs 87.27 crore in the three months ended June 30, 2025, FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. These losses were attributed to the ramp-up of the Ranchi and Srinagar hospitals and increased fixed and operating expenses following the expansion of bed capacity at the Ranchi hospital. Any failure of these subsidiaries to achieve profitability or raise adequate capital to meet their obligations could adversely affect the company’s financial performance.

The company reported employee attrition rates of 12.01%, 16.09%, 60.38%, 66.74%, and 65.27% in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and June 30, 2025, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. The shortage of skilled healthcare professionals and competition for talent may increase recruitment, training, and staff costs, while high attrition or the premature termination of visiting doctors’ arrangements could affect service quality, patient intake, and hospital utilisation.

Five of the company’s eight hospitals are located in North India, which contributed 68.07%, 66.89%, 66.07%, 68.40%, and 67.33% of revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and June 30, 2025, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any adverse regional economic conditions, changes in healthcare demand, regulatory developments, natural disasters or security disruptions affecting these hospitals could disrupt operations and adversely affect the company’s business and financial performance.

The company generated 74.35%, 75.30%, 74.70%, 71.92%, and 72.34% of its revenue from operations from cardiac sciences, oncology sciences, neurosciences, gastro sciences, orthopaedics and sports injury, and renal sciences in the three months ended June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any decline in patient demand, loss of key specialists, increased competition, or the need for costly upgrades to medical technology and training could affect revenue from these specialities and adversely impact the company’s financial performance.

As of June 30, 2026, the company had contingent liabilities of Rs 398.44 crore, equivalent to 89.55% of its net worth, primarily comprising corporate guarantees of Rs 376.40 crore and claims against the group not acknowledged as debts of Rs 11.79 crore. These liabilities include claims relating to patient negligence, income tax, and GST, as well as guarantees provided in connection with credit facilities. If a significant portion of these debts materialise, it could hurt the company’s cash flows, financial condition and results of operations.

The company, its subsidiaries, promoter, directors, key managerial personnel and senior management are involved in outstanding litigation, while certain regulatory and statutory proceedings have also been initiated against the promoter and directors in the past. Any adverse decisions in these proceedings or similar future cases could result in penalties and adversely affect the company’s business, cash flows and reputation

The company generated 78.25%, 78.93%, 78.26%, 79.46%, and 81.71% of its revenue from operations through its in-patient department in the three months ended June 30, 2026, and June 30, 2025, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Its bed occupancy rate declined from 52.46% in FY24 to 50.78% in FY25 before increasing to 61.75% in FY26. Any inability to sustain occupancy levels or attract patients could affect revenue, the absorption of fixed costs and profitability.

As of August 31, 2026, the company and its subsidiaries had aggregate secured borrowings of Rs 990.33 crore. The company’s reliance on borrowings to finance working capital, hospital facilities and medical equipment exposes it to repayment obligations and financing costs, which could adversely affect its cash flows and financial condition if operating cash flows are insufficient to meet these obligations.

ipos.name: Jio Platforms
ipos.about:
Jio Platforms is a technology company that provides digital connectivity and digital services across India. Its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited, offers mobile connectivity, fixed broadband, and digital services. These services provide access to the internet, digital applications, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI). 
The company develops and operates its own technology stack, covering network infrastructure, device engineering, software, operating systems, and digital applications. Its technology portfolio includes 4G, 5G, cloud-native core network architectures, and AI-driven network automation. The company also develops digital products and technologies for consumers and businesses. 
As of June 30, 2026, Jio Platforms and its subsidiaries had applied for 7,220 patents in India and other countries across various digital technology areas. The company had 12,477 employees in its digital products and technology development team as of the same date. Its business combines digital connectivity infrastructure with software, applications, and other digital services.
Use of proceeds: 
This is a fresh issue of shares. Therefore, the net proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company. They will be utilised for the following purposes:
Prepayment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by the material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL) — Rs 27,500 crore
General corporate purposes
strengths: Jio Platforms claims to have vertically integrated technology capabilities across network infrastructure, device engineering, software, operating systems, and digital applications. As of June 30, 2026, the company and its subsidiaries had applied for 7,220 patents in India and foreign jurisdictions, including technologies related to 4G, 5G, 6G, and AI-driven network automation.

The company claims to operate an end-to-end 5G standalone technology stack nationwide, covering its core network, devices, and OSS/BSS operating systems. It also uses proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology to provide fixed wireless broadband connectivity, with bandwidth of up to 1 Gbps.

As of June 30, 2026, the company had access to a pan-India network comprising 360,537 network towers and over 1.0 million route kilometres of fibre. Its wireless broadband network covered more than 99% of India’s population, while its fixed broadband coverage extended to approximately 98% of the country’s pin codes.

The company offers fixed broadband services through JioFiber and JioAirFiber. As of June 30, 2026, these services had a combined customer base of 28.6 million, while JioAirFiber had approximately 14.0 million customers.

Jio Platforms offers consumer applications such as MyJio, JioTV+, JioSaavn, JioAICloud, and JioGames, along with business solutions such as managed Wi-Fi and hybrid cloud services. As of June 30, 2026, JioTV+ aggregated over 1,000 digital TV channels and 15 OTT services.

The company uses its proprietary AI platform, JioBrain, for network capacity allocation, fault prediction, anomaly detection, and network optimisation. It also uses digital twin technology to assess network coverage, plan infrastructure rollouts, and guide field engineers during customer installations.
The company reported revenue from operations of Rs 146,885.3 crore and EBITDA of Rs 76,255.4 crore in FY26. Its net leverage ratio declined from 0.88 times in FY24 to 0.36 times in FY26.
risks: Jio Platforms has entered into various agreements with Reliance Industries Limited, Reliance Retail Limited, and other Reliance Group entities for project execution, business support, equipment supply, and distribution services. Reliance Retail Limited is the sole distributor of the company’s prepaid connectivity services, which contributed 76.37%, 77.88%, 77.08%, 78.57%, and 79.35% of consolidated revenue from operations in the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, and FY26, FY25, and FY24, respectively. Any disruption or termination of these arrangements could adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL), the company’s material subsidiary, contributed 87.74% of consolidated revenue from operations, 94.88% of EBITDA, and 93.76% of profit after tax in FY26. For the three months ended June 30, 2026, its contribution was 87.34%, 93.89%, and 92.31%, respectively. Any deterioration in RJIL’s business or financial performance due to competition, regulatory changes, technological disruption, or other adverse events could materially affect the company’s consolidated financial results. Further, the company’s key performance indicators primarily reflect RJIL’s digital connectivity services and may not adequately represent its technology platform business, potentially limiting investors’ ability to assess its performance in this area.

Jio Platforms depends on a limited number of service providers for passive network infrastructure. As of June 30, 2026, Summit Digitel Infrastructure Limited owned 174,451 of the 360,537 network towers used by the company, while Jio Digital Fibre Private Limited met approximately 98% of its optic fibre network requirements, excluding the last-mile fibre network owned by RJIL. RJIL has long-term agreements with both providers, which require minimum payments and do not permit termination by RJIL. Any disruption in tower or fibre availability, failure to meet service commitments, or relocation of infrastructure could cause network outages, service degradation, and customer losses, adversely affecting the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms’ systems, networks, applications, and data may be exposed to cybersecurity threats, including ransomware, phishing, malware, and data or privacy breaches. Although the company reported no successful cyberattacks or security breaches during the three months ended June 30, 2026, or FY24 to FY26, future incidents could require significant expenditure to investigate and resolve, disrupt operations, and damage its reputation. The company also relies on data centre infrastructure provided by its promoter in Jamnagar, Nagpur, and Mumbai, as well as third-party cloud hosting and edge infrastructure services. Any disruption or termination of these arrangements could affect service quality, increase customer churn, and adversely affect the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms’ telecommunications business is subject to extensive and evolving regulations covering licensing, spectrum usage, data privacy, and digital services. RJIL faces regulatory demands, including Rs 27.1 crore in financial disincentives imposed by TRAI for alleged violations relating to unsolicited commercial communications and service quality, which are under appeal. RJIL also faces a disputed additional spectrum usage charge demand of Rs 138.91 crore, which was set aside by TDSAT but is subject to an appeal before the Supreme Court. The company has previously incurred Rs 123.2 crore in non-performance penalties and liquidated damages for prolonged service interruptions in specified locations. Changes in licence fees, spectrum charges or other regulations, or failure to comply with applicable requirements, could increase costs, result in penalties or restrict services, adversely affecting the company’s business and financial performance.

Jio Platforms operates a capital-intensive business, with cash capital expenditure of Rs 34,184.3 crore in FY26, Rs 44,268 crore in FY25 and Rs 53,509.6 crore in FY24, representing 23.27%, 34.53% and 48.84% of revenue from operations, respectively. In FY26, network expenditure accounted for Rs 29,377.1 crore of cash capital expenditure. Significant spending on network expansion, technology upgrades, and digital platforms may take time to generate returns and depends on regulatory approvals, funding availability, and customer adoption. Cost overruns, delays, or lower-than-expected demand for new services could reduce the returns on these investments and adversely affect the company’s financial performance.

Fifteen subsidiaries of Jio Platforms incurred losses during the three months ended June 30, 2026, with combined losses after tax of Rs 20.5 crore. In FY26, 11 subsidiaries reported combined losses after tax of Rs 100.6 crore, compared with Rs 162.8 crore in FY25 and Rs 57.4 crore in FY24. Although these losses were not material to the company’s consolidated financial results during these periods, continued losses may require additional financial support or equity infusions by the company and could adversely affect its financial condition and results of operations.

ipos.name: Zetwerk
ipos.about:
Zetwerk Ltd is a technology-led manufacturing platform that serves industrial and consumer goods customers in India and international markets. The company aggregates manufacturing capacity through a network of third-party suppliers and its own facilities, supported by its proprietary technology platform, Zetwerk OS. Its customers operate across industries such as utilities, renewable energy, consumer electronics, artificial intelligence infrastructure, aerospace, space and defence, oil and gas, and industrial automation. 
The company offers access to manufacturing processes including sheet metal stamping, metal fabrication, injection moulding, extrusion, assembly, die casting, forging, grinding and machining. Its third-party supplier network spans several countries, including India, Vietnam, Thailand, Taiwan, Germany, Spain, Mexico and the USA. Zetwerk serves customers ranging from startups to established companies across various industries. Since its incorporation, the company has cumulatively delivered products and raw materials worth Rs 74,374.21 crore in gross merchandise value (GMV) to its customers.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO consists of both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS).​ Proceeds from the OFS will go to the respective selling shareholders, whereas the net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised for the following purposes:​
Repayment/prepayment, in part or full, of certain of or all of borrowings availed by: (a) the company; (b) certain of its subsidiaries, namely, (i) Sharp Tanks and Structurals Private Limited; (ii) Terra91 International Private Limited; (iii) Smile Electronics Limited; (iv) Kryfs Power Components Limited; (v) Kryfs Transformers Private Limited; (vi) Unimacts Global LLC; (vii) Zetwerk Manufacturing SG Pte. Ltd.; (viii) Zap91 Solar India Private Limited; and (ix) Zet Town India Private Limited through investments in such them — Rs 1,300 crore
Funding inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and other strategic acquisitions, and general corporate purposes
strengths: In FY26, Zetwerk had a network of 6,979 third-party suppliers across 26 countries and 26 manufacturing facilities across four countries, including India. Its manufacturing capabilities cover multiple processes, allowing it to produce products ranging from individual components to complete assemblies and finished goods.

The company serves industries including utilities, renewable energy, electrical equipment, infrastructure, transportation, aerospace, defence, industrial automation and space technology. Its manufacturing business also caters to demand for both capital expenditure-related products and recurring operational components, reducing its dependence on a single industry or demand type.

Zetwerk operates its manufacturing platform through Zetwerk OS, its proprietary technology system. The platform covers enquiry management, supplier selection, design for manufacturing, order management, production planning, quality management, inventory tracking and logistics coordination across multiple suppliers and locations.

Zetwerk’s Manufacturing Order Book stood at Rs 12,370.01 crore as of March 31, 2026, compared with Rs 8,628.98 crore as of March 31, 2025, and Rs 6,169.75 crore as of March 31, 2024. The company also reported an order book of Rs 13,062.40 crore as of June 30, 2026.

Through its Ecosystem Business segment, operating under the Terra91 brand, the company aggregates material demand from customers and suppliers to negotiate with raw material suppliers. This business supports bulk purchasing, pre-negotiated procurement terms and quality checks on raw materials.
risks: The company reported losses from continuing operations of Rs 964.39 crore in FY26, Rs 215.07 crore in FY25, and Rs 852.53 crore in FY24. It also reported losses from discontinued operations of Rs 641.78 crore in FY26, Rs 155.64 crore in FY25, and Rs 65.42 crore in FY24. If the company is unable to generate adequate revenue and manage its expenses, continued losses may adversely affect its financial condition, cash flows, and business operations.

The company relies on third-party suppliers for 80.46% of its combined Manufacturing and Ecosystem Business segment revenue in FY26, compared with 84.11% in FY25 and 96.51% in FY24. Its procurement arrangements are generally based on short-term purchase orders without fixed long-term commitments, while its just-in-time procurement model and limited buffer inventories increase its exposure to supply disruptions, quality issues and raw material price fluctuations. Any inability to secure supplies on acceptable terms or pass increased costs on to customers could adversely affect its business and profit margins.

The company’s top 10 suppliers accounted for expenses of Rs 6,163.12 crore in FY26, Rs 4,574.02 crore in FY25 and Rs 4,736.59 crore in FY24, representing 38.18%, 39.59% and 36.87% of its total expenses for continuing operations, respectively. Its supplier arrangements are primarily based on short-term purchase orders without fixed long-term commitments. Supply shortages, capacity constraints, labour unrest, natural disasters or quality issues could disrupt manufacturing and deliveries, increase costs, and adversely affect the company’s business, financial condition and reputation.

The company’s top 10 customers contributed revenue of Rs 5,713.56 crore in FY26, Rs 3,046.70 crore in FY25 and Rs 2,765.88 crore in FY24, accounting for 35.90%, 26.89% and 22.37% of revenue from continuing operations, respectively. Although the company had 1,802 customers in FY26 and did not lose any key customers during FY24 to FY26 or the three months ended June 30, 2026, its business remains exposed to changes in demand from major customers. Reduced customer spending, financial difficulties, changes in procurement strategies, or failure to secure replacement orders could adversely affect its revenue, cash flows, and financial condition.

The company reported negative operating cash flows of Rs 681.53 crore in FY26, Rs 386.28 crore in FY25, and Rs 281.54 crore in FY24, as well as Rs 506.18 crore and Rs 796.40 crore for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and June 30, 2025, respectively. These outflows were primarily due to working capital changes, including increases in other financial and current assets and trade receivables, and decreases in trade payables and acceptances. If negative operating cash flows persist, the company may face difficulties funding working capital and capital expenditure requirements, meeting financing obligations and obtaining additional financing, which could adversely affect its business and financial condition.

ipos.name: Sahajanand Medical Technologies
ipos.about:
Sahajanand Medical Technologies Limited develops, manufactures, and sells medical devices used in vascular and structural heart interventions. Founded in 2001, the company offers vascular intervention products, including coronary stents and coronary balloon catheters, and structural heart products, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) devices and occluders. Its portfolio also includes renal stents, peripheral drug-coated balloons, and traded medical products.
The company markets its products through direct sales, hybrid, and distributor-led models. In FY26, it generated revenue from 77 countries, including India, with operations across Europe and other international markets. It currently operates three manufacturing facilities, two in India and one in Thailand. Additionally, it has two research and development centres, located in India and Thailand, focused on medical device development and product improvements.
Use of proceeds: 
The IPO is an offer-for-sale (OFS). The company will not receive any proceeds from the offer. Net proceeds from the offer will go to the promoter selling shareholders in proportion to the number of shares offered by them for sale.
The primary objective of the offer is to achieve the benefits of listing the equity shares on the stock exchanges, which is expected to enhance the company’s visibility and brand recognition. Listing will also provide liquidity to the existing shareholders and create a public market for the company’s shares in India​.
strengths: According to the F&S Report, Sahajanand Medical Technologies held nearly 25% of India's drug-eluting stents (DES) market by sales volume in FY26. The company was also among the top five by DES sales volume in Germany, Spain, Poland, and Brazil as of March 31, 2026.

The company marketed its products in 77 countries, including India, in FY26. Its international revenue from operations increased from Rs 587.84 crore in FY24 to Rs 704.23 crore in FY25 and Rs 894.20 crore in FY26, representing a CAGR of 23.34%.

The company operates two R&D centres in Surat, India, and Nonthaburi, Thailand. As of the RHP date, it had 119 granted patents globally, 78 pending patent applications, and five design registrations in India. Its R&D expenditure stood at 9.04%, 9.07%, and 8.61% of revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively.

The company claims to have an extensive clinical research portfolio supporting its medical devices. As of June 30, 2026, its products were supported by 75 clinical studies, including 66 completed and nine ongoing studies, with research on its products published in medical journals such as The Lancet and The New England Journal of Medicine.

The company operates three manufacturing facilities in Surat, Hyderabad, and Thailand. All three facilities hold ISO 13485:2016 certification for medical device quality management systems. Its facilities also hold various regulatory approvals and certifications, including CDSCO, CE, ANVISA, TGA Australia, and Korean GMP, depending on the facility.

The company claims to have integrated manufacturing capabilities, including in-house production of balloon catheters, laser cutting, electropolishing, drug and polymer coating, and valve manufacturing. It also reported that approximately 33% of the available area at its Hyderabad facility was being utilised, providing space for future expansion.

The company has completed acquisitions to expand its product portfolio and international distribution network. Its acquisitions of Vascular Concepts and Vascular Innovations enabled its entry into structural heart devices, while the acquisitions of Imex in Spain and Zarek in Brazil strengthened its distribution operations. Revenue from Imex and Zarek grew at CAGRs of 52.10% and 23.91%, respectively, since their acquisition in FY20.
risks: The company's revenue from vascular intervention (VI) devices stood at Rs 618.27 crore (68.57%), Rs 674.97 crore (65.86%), and Rs 740.09 crore (61.14%) in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Additionally, its Supraflex Cruz product contributed Rs 431.35 crore (47.84%), Rs 431.03 crore (42.06%), and Rs 450.00 crore (37.17%) to revenue from operations during the same periods, respectively. Any decline in demand for these products or increased competition could adversely affect the company's revenue and profitability.

The company's top 10 suppliers accounted for purchases worth Rs 164.57 crore (58.88%), Rs 170.75 crore (64.37%), and Rs 184.72 crore (59.15%) in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. The company also depends on a limited number of suppliers, including single suppliers for certain critical materials, and does not enter into long-term supply agreements. Any supply disruption or increase in raw material prices could adversely affect its manufacturing operations and profitability.

The company's imports accounted for Rs 207.60 crore (74.28%), Rs 195.41 crore (73.67%), and Rs 241.00 crore (77.18%) of its total purchases in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Its dependence on imported raw materials and components from countries including Germany, China, the Netherlands, and Ireland exposes it to foreign exchange fluctuations, import restrictions, and supply chain disruptions, which could negatively impact its operations and financial performance.

The company's revenue from customers outside India stood at Rs 587.84 crore (65.20%), Rs 704.23 crore (68.71%), and Rs 894.20 crore (73.87%) in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Since a significant portion of its revenue and purchases is denominated in foreign currencies, adverse exchange rate movements could affect its profitability and financial condition.

The company's top 10 distributors contributed Rs 237.47 crore (26.34%), Rs 215.34 crore (21.01%), and Rs 190.12 crore (15.71%) to revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. The company generally does not enter into long-term agreements with its distributors, and certain international product registrations are held in their names. Any loss of key distributors or termination of these arrangements could adversely affect its sales and market presence.

The company has experienced underutilisation of certain manufacturing capacities. In FY26, capacity utilisation for stents at its Hyderabad facility stood at 64.26%, while utilisation for drug-coated PTCA balloon catheters at its Surat facility was just 1.81%. Continued underutilisation of manufacturing facilities could increase operating costs and adversely affect the company's profitability.

The company has faced regulatory challenges in certain international markets. Its subsidiary in Brazil had a product registration cancelled following a classification dispute, while its applications for Hydra TAVI in Taiwan and Australia were rejected and required additional testing or clinical studies. Any delay or failure in obtaining the required regulatory approvals could restrict the company's ability to sell its products in these markets.

The company has received notices from regulatory authorities regarding its operations. Its subsidiary received a notice from the Telangana Pollution Control Board in December 2024 concerning effluent disposal, while the company received a notice from the Assistant Drug Controller and Licensing Authority in May 2024 regarding discrepancies at its premises, with the latter matter remaining pending as disclosed in the RHP. Any adverse regulatory action could result in penalties, suspension of licences or disruption of manufacturing operations.

The company reported a consolidated loss of Rs 7.35 crore in FY24 and standalone losses of Rs 34.46 crore and Rs 7.92 crore in FY24 and FY25, respectively. Additionally, certain subsidiaries, including SMT Switzerland AG and Vascular Innovations Co Ltd have reported losses in recent periods. Continued losses at these entities could require additional financial support from the company and adversely affect its consolidated financial position.

The company's average working capital stood at Rs 263.91 crore, Rs 254.25 crore, and Rs 291.44 crore in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. As of June 30, 2026, it had outstanding working capital loans amounting to Rs 240.99 crore. Inability to generate sufficient internal funds or obtain additional working capital financing could adversely affect its operations and financial condition.

The company incurred substantial research and development expenditure amounting to Rs 81.46 crore (9.04%), Rs 92.99 crore (9.07%), and Rs 104.16 crore (8.61%) of revenue from operations in FY24, FY25, and FY26, respectively. Any failure to successfully develop, obtain regulatory approval for or commercialise new products could result in unrecovered R&D expenditure and adversely affect the company's profitability.

The company's trade receivables stood at Rs 215.17 crore, Rs 263.48 crore, and Rs 286.25 crore as of March 31, 2024, 2025, and 2026, respectively. As of June 30, 2026, its trade receivables stood at Rs 306.56 crore. Any delay or default in receiving payments from customers or distributors could adversely affect the company's cash flows, profitability and financial condition.

The company, its subsidiaries, directors, and promoters are involved in certain outstanding legal proceedings. Any adverse judgments in these cases could negatively impact the company's business, reputation and financial position
As of June 30, 2026, the company had outstanding financial indebtedness of Rs 320.63 crore. Any failure to service or repay these loans can harm the company’s operations and financial position.
